metadata.title: On the exponents of distribution of primes and smooth numbers

extraction_notes.note: assumption or definition: the 'Assumption' environment defines when a tuple satisfies the exceptional large sieve condition, so it is typed definition.
equation or theorem: numbered equations (1.1) and (3.3) are named in the text as the Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem and the Kim–Sarnak bound, so they are external theorems.
The heuristic outline of Section 2 (sentences deriving the conditional and unconditional exponents) is not extracted as prose nodes; only its numbered equations are kept.
The proof of the twin-prime corollary rests on a table of numerically computed sieve integrals from an adapted Mathematica file; the table is kept inside the proof step.
Parts (i) and (ii) of Theorem 1.3 are proved in separate places but no node relies on a single part, so they are encoded as `parts` rather than nested claims; both proofs point at the theorem.
Most proofs adapt arguments of Maynard, Lichtman and Drappeau by citation, so many steps only describe changes to external computations.

nodes.statement: Let $q$ be a large positive integer, $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ have $(a, q) = 1$, and $A > 0$. The Siegel--Walfisz theorem gives a pointwise asymptotic for the number of primes up to $x$ which are congruent to $a$ modulo $q$, \[ \pi(x, q; a) \sim \frac{\pi(x)}{\varphi(q)}, \qquad \text{ as } x \to \infty, \text{ for } q \le (\log x)^A, \] where $\pi(x) := \#\{\text{prime } p \le x\}$ and $\pi(x, q; a) := \#\{\text{prime } p \le x : p \equiv a \pmod{q}\}$.
nodes.name: Siegel–Walfisz theorem
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise asymptotic $\pi(x,q;a)\sim\pi(x)/\varphi(q)$ for moduli $q\le(\log x)^A$; defines the prime-counting functions.
assumptions: $q$ be a large positive integer, $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ have $(a, q) = 1$, and $A > 0$
conclusions: The Siegel--Walfisz theorem gives a pointwise asymptotic for the number of primes up to $x$ which are congruent to $a$ modulo $q$, \[ \pi(x, q; a) \sim \frac{\pi(x)}{\varphi(q)}, \qquad \text{ as } x \to \infty, \text{ for } q \le (\log x)^A,

nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{q \le x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B} \\ (q, a) = 1}} \left\vert \pi(x; q, a) - \frac{\pi(x)}{\varphi(q)}\right\vert \ll_A \frac{x}{(\log x)^A}.
nodes.name: Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem
nodes.statement_short: Primes are equidistributed in APs on average over moduli up to $x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B}$.
assumptions: for $B = B(A)$ large enough in terms of $A$
conclusions: \sum_{\substack{q \le x^{1/2}(\log x)^{-B} \\ (q, a) = 1}} \left\vert \pi(x; q, a) - \frac{\pi(x)}{\varphi(q)}\right\vert \ll_A \frac{x}{(\log x)^A}.
nodes.label: eq:bv

nodes.statement: Overcoming the square-root barrier at $q < x^{1/2}$, i.e., going ``beyond GRH'' on average, remains a central open problem in analytic number theory.
nodes.name: Square-root barrier for primes in arithmetic progressions

nodes.statement: Elliot--Halberstam \cite{elliott1968conjecture} conjectured that the same estimate holds true in the optimal range of moduli $q \le x^{1-\varepsilon}$, and Polymath8b \cite{polymath2014variants} showed that a generalization of this conjecture would imply the existence of infinitely many pairs of primes with distance at most $6$.
nodes.name: Elliott–Halberstam conjecture
nodes.statement_short: Bombieri–Vinogradov-type estimate should hold for moduli up to $x^{1-\varepsilon}$; a generalization implies bounded gaps $\le 6$.
conclusions: the same estimate holds true in the optimal range of moduli $q \le x^{1-\varepsilon}$

nodes.statement: If such an analogue of \cref{eq:bv} holds with a weighted sum over all $q \le x^\vartheta$, for any fixed residue $a$, then we say that the primes have \emph{exponent of distribution} $\vartheta \in (0, 1)$ (or \emph{level of distribution} $x^\vartheta$) with respect to the weights $(\lambda_q)$.
nodes.name: Exponent of distribution
nodes.statement_short: Primes have exponent of distribution $\vartheta$ w.r.t. weights $(\lambda_q)$ if a weighted Bombieri–Vinogradov bound holds for all $q\le x^\vartheta$.

nodes.statement: Motivated by a `well-factorable' variant of the linear sieve weights \cite{iwaniec1980new,fouvry1983primes}, Bombieri--Friedlander--Iwaniec \cite[Theorem 10]{bombieri1986primes} considered sequences $(\lambda_q)$ that can be expressed as a Dirichlet convolution of two sequences of any pre-specified lengths, and achieved an exponent of distribution of $\tfrac{4}{7}-\varepsilon$ in this setting.
nodes.name: Bombieri–Friedlander–Iwaniec theorem for well-factorable weights
nodes.statement_short: Exponent of distribution $4/7-\varepsilon$ for primes with well-factorable weights.

nodes.statement: A complex sequence $(\lambda_q)_{q \le Q}$ is said to be \emph{triply-well-factorable} of level $Q$ iff for any $Q_1, Q_2, Q_3 \ge 1$ with $Q_1 Q_2 Q_3 = Q$, there exist $1$-bounded complex sequences $(\alpha_{q_1})$, $(\beta_{q_2})$, $(\gamma_{q_3})$ supported on $q_i \le Q_i$, such that for all $q$, \[ \lambda_q = \sum_{q = q_1 q_2 q_3} \alpha_{q_1} \beta_{q_2} \gamma_{q_3}. \]
nodes.name: Triply-well-factorable weights
differentia: for any $Q_1, Q_2, Q_3 \ge 1$ with $Q_1 Q_2 Q_3 = Q$, there exist $1$-bounded complex sequences $(\alpha_{q_1})$, $(\beta_{q_2})$, $(\gamma_{q_3})$ supported on $q_i \le Q_i$, such that for all $q$,
nodes.statement_short: $(\lambda_q)$ of level $Q$ factors as a triple convolution of 1-bounded sequences supported on $q_i\le Q_i$ for any $Q_1Q_2Q_3=Q$.
nodes.label: def:triply-well-fact

nodes.statement: For such weights, which arise in a slight variant of the $\beta$-sieve with $\beta \ge 2$, Maynard \cite[Theorem 1.1]{maynard2025primes2} achieved the exponent of distribution $\tfrac{3}{5} - \varepsilon$ (i.e., with a level $Q = x^{3/5-\varepsilon}$).
nodes.name: Maynard's theorem for triply-well-factorable weights
nodes.origin_citation: Maynard, Primes in APs to large moduli II, Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement_short: Exponent of distribution $3/5-\varepsilon$ for triply-well-factorable weights.

nodes.statement: His results also implied an improved exponent of $\tfrac{7}{12}-\varepsilon$ for the well-factorable variant of the upper-bound linear sieve weights (the case $\beta = 1$), which are close to being triply-well-factorable.
nodes.name: Maynard's exponent 7/12 for well-factorable linear sieve weights
nodes.origin_citation: Maynard, Primes in APs to large moduli II
nodes.statement_short: Exponent $7/12-\varepsilon$ for the well-factorable upper-bound linear sieve weights.

nodes.statement: In this context, Lichtman \cite{lichtman2023primes} used optimized Deshouillers--Iwaniec-style estimates, via Kim--Sarnak's bound \cite{kim2003functoriality}, to improve the exponent of distribution for triply-well-factorable weights to $\tfrac{66}{107} - \varepsilon \approx 0.6168$ unconditionally, and up to $\tfrac{5}{8} - \varepsilon = 0.625 - \varepsilon$ assuming:
nodes.name: Lichtman's exponent 66/107 for triply-well-factorable weights
nodes.statement_short: Exponent $66/107-\varepsilon$ unconditionally and $5/8-\varepsilon$ under Selberg's conjecture, for triply-well-factorable weights.

nodes.statement: All eigenvalues of the hyperbolic Laplacian on Maass forms for congruence subgroups $\Gamma_0(q)$ are at least equal to $1/4$.
nodes.name: Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture
conclusions: All eigenvalues of the hyperbolic Laplacian on Maass forms for congruence subgroups $\Gamma_0(q)$ are at least equal to $1/4$.
nodes.label: conj:selberg

nodes.statement: Let $a \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, $A, \varepsilon > 0$, $x \ge 2$. Assume either: \begin{itemize} \item[$(i)$.] $Q \le x^{5/8-\varepsilon}$, and $(\lambda_q)$ are triply-well-factorable weights of level $Q$, or \item[$(ii)$.] $Q \le x^{3/5-\varepsilon}$, and $(\lambda_q)$ are the upper-bound well-factorable linear sieve weights of level $Q$. \end{itemize} (See \cref{def:linear-sieve} for part $(ii)$.) Then one has \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{q \le Q \\ (q, a) = 1}} \lambda_q \left(\pi(x; q, a) - \frac{\pi(x)}{\varphi(q)}\right) \ll_{\varepsilon,A,a} \frac{x}{(\log x)^A}. \end{equation}
nodes.name: Primes in APs to large moduli
nodes.statement_short: Primes have exponent of distribution $5/8-\varepsilon$ with triply-well-factorable weights, and $3/5-\varepsilon$ with well-factorable upper-bound linear sieve weights.
assumptions: Let $a \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, $A, \varepsilon > 0$, $x \ge 2$
$Q \le x^{5/8-\varepsilon}$, and $(\lambda_q)$ are triply-well-factorable weights of level $Q$
$Q \le x^{3/5-\varepsilon}$, and $(\lambda_q)$ are the upper-bound well-factorable linear sieve weights of level $Q$
conclusions: Then one has \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{q \le Q \\ (q, a) = 1}} \lambda_q \left(\pi(x; q, a) - \frac{\pi(x)}{\varphi(q)}\right) \ll_{\varepsilon,A,a} \frac{x}{(\log x)^A}. \end{equation}

conclusions: Then one has \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{q \le Q \\ (q, a) = 1}} \lambda_q \left(\pi(x; q, a) - \frac{\pi(x)}{\varphi(q)}\right) \ll_{\varepsilon,A,a} \frac{x}{(\log x)^A}. \end{equation}

assumptions: $Q \le x^{3/5-\varepsilon}$, and $(\lambda_q)$ are the upper-bound well-factorable linear sieve weights of level $Q$
conclusions: Then one has \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{q \le Q \\ (q, a) = 1}} \lambda_q \left(\pi(x; q, a) - \frac{\pi(x)}{\varphi(q)}\right) \ll_{\varepsilon,A,a} \frac{x}{(\log x)^A}. \end{equation}

nodes.label: thm:primes

nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{q \le Q \\ (q, a) = 1}} \lambda_q \left(\pi(x; q, a) - \frac{\pi(x)}{\varphi(q)}\right) \ll_{\varepsilon,A,a} \frac{x}{(\log x)^A}.
nodes.name: Weighted equidistribution of primes in APs (1.2)
nodes.label: eq:primes-in-ap

nodes.statement: As $x \to \infty$, one has \[ \#\{p \le x : p, p+2 \text{ are prime}\} \le (3.203 + o(1))\, \Pi_2(x), \] where $\Pi_2(x) := \tfrac{2x}{(\log x)^2} \prod_{p > 2} \tfrac{1 - 2/p}{(1 - 1/p)^2}$ is the asymptotic predicted by Hardy--Littlewood \cite{hardy1923problems}.
nodes.name: Count of twin primes
nodes.statement_short: The number of twin primes up to $x$ is at most $(3.203+o(1))$ times the Hardy–Littlewood prediction $\Pi_2(x)$.
assumptions: As $x \to \infty$,
conclusions: one has \[ \#\{p \le x : p, p+2 \text{ are prime}\} \le (3.203 + o(1))\, \Pi_2(x), \] where $\Pi_2(x) := \tfrac{2x}{(\log x)^2} \prod_{p > 2} \tfrac{1 - 2/p}{(1 - 1/p)^2}$ is the asymptotic predicted by Hardy--Littlewood \cite{hardy1923problems}.
nodes.label: cor:twin-primes

nodes.statement: The analogous equidistribution problem for \emph{smooth} numbers \cite{fouvry1996repartition,drappeau2015theoremes} concerns the quantities \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} \Psi(x, y) := \# \{n \le x : P^+(n) \le y\}, \qquad\quad \Psi_q(x, y) := \# \{n \le x : P^+(n) \le y,\ (n, q) = 1\}, \\ \Psi(x, y; a, q) := \# \{n \le x : P^+(n) \le y,\ n \equiv a \pmod{q}\}, \end{gathered} \end{equation} where $P^+(n)$ denotes the largest prime factor of $n$; the key setting is $y \le x^{1/C}$, with $C$ large.
nodes.name: Smooth number counting functions
nodes.statement_short: Counts of $y$-smooth integers up to $x$: all, coprime to $q$, and in the residue class $a$ mod $q$.

nodes.statement: \begin{gathered} \Psi(x, y) := \# \{n \le x : P^+(n) \le y\}, \qquad\quad \Psi_q(x, y) := \# \{n \le x : P^+(n) \le y,\ (n, q) = 1\}, \\ \Psi(x, y; a, q) := \# \{n \le x : P^+(n) \le y,\ n \equiv a \pmod{q}\}, \end{gathered}
nodes.name: Smooth number counting functions (1.3)
nodes.label: eq:smooth-notations

nodes.statement: In this context, Granville \cite[Theorem 2]{granville1993integers} proved a suitable analogue of the Bombieri--Vinogradov theorem, achieving the exponent of distribution $\tfrac{1}{2}-\varepsilon$ (see also \cite{wolke1973mittlereI,wolke1973mittlereII,fouvry1991entiers,granville1993integers2}).
nodes.name: Granville's Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem for smooth numbers
nodes.statement_short: Smooth numbers have exponent of distribution $1/2-\varepsilon$.

nodes.statement: Relying on a triple convolution estimate of Bombieri--Friedlander--Iwaniec \cite[Theorem 4]{bombieri1986primes}, Fouvry--Tenenbaum \cite{fouvry1996repartition} raised the exponent to $\tfrac{3}{5}-\varepsilon$, with an upper bound of $x (\log x)^{-A}$ as in \cref{eq:bv}.
nodes.name: Fouvry–Tenenbaum exponent 3/5 for smooth numbers
nodes.statement_short: Smooth numbers have exponent of distribution $3/5-\varepsilon$, with error $x(\log x)^{-A}$.

nodes.statement: Drappeau later \cite{drappeau2015theoremes} strengthened the bound back to $\Psi(x, y)(\log x)^{-A}$, with the same exponent of $\tfrac{3}{5}-\varepsilon$.
nodes.name: Drappeau's theorem for smooth numbers
nodes.statement_short: Exponent $3/5-\varepsilon$ for smooth numbers with error $\Psi(x,y)(\log x)^{-A}$.

nodes.statement: Using a different arrangement of exponential sums and optimized Deshouillers--Iwaniec-style estimates, the author \cite{pascadi2023smooth} recently showed that smooth numbers have exponent of distribution $\tfrac{66}{107} - \varepsilon \approx 0.6168$, and up to $\tfrac{5}{8} - \varepsilon = 0.625 - \varepsilon$ assuming Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture.
nodes.name: Smooth numbers have exponent of distribution 66/107
nodes.statement_short: Smooth numbers have exponent $66/107-\varepsilon$, and $5/8-\varepsilon$ under Selberg's conjecture.

nodes.statement: Let $a \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$ and $A, \varepsilon > 0$, $x \ge 2$. Then there exists a large enough $C = C(a, A, \varepsilon) > 0$ such that for any $y \in [(\log x)^C, x^{1/C}]$ and $Q \le x^{5/8 - \varepsilon}$, one has \[ \sum_{\substack{q \le Q \\ (q, a) = 1}} \left\vert \Psi(x, y; a, q) - \frac{\Psi_q(x, y)}{\varphi(q)} \right\vert \ll_{\varepsilon,A,a} \frac{\Psi(x, y)}{(\log x)^A}. \]
nodes.name: Smooth numbers in APs to large moduli
nodes.statement_short: Smooth numbers have exponent of distribution $5/8-\varepsilon$ with absolute values (arbitrary weights).
assumptions: Let $a \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$ and $A, \varepsilon > 0$, $x \ge 2$.
conclusions: Then there exists a large enough $C = C(a, A, \varepsilon) > 0$ such that for any $y \in [(\log x)^C, x^{1/C}]$ and $Q \le x^{5/8 - \varepsilon}$, one has \[ \sum_{\substack{q \le Q \\ (q, a) = 1}} \left\vert \Psi(x, y; a, q) - \frac{\Psi_q(x, y)}{\varphi(q)} \right\vert \ll_{\varepsilon,A,a} \frac{\Psi(x, y)}{(\log x)^A}. \]

nodes.statement: One can extend \cref{thm:smooth} to smooth-supported multiplicative functions, using our triple convolution estimate (\cref{prop:triple-convo}) in the work of Drappeau--Granville--Shao \cite{drappeau2017smooth}.

nodes.statement: For any $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $C > 0$ such that for any $x \ge 2$ and $y \in [(\log x)^C, x^{1/C}]$, one has \[ \#\{n \le x : P^+(n), P^+(n+1) \le y\} \ll_\varepsilon \varrho(u)^{1 + 5/8-\varepsilon}, \] where $u := (\log x)/\log y$ and $\varrho$ denotes the Dickman function \cite{hildebrand1986number}.
nodes.name: Count of consecutive smooth numbers
nodes.statement_short: The number of $n\le x$ with $n,n+1$ both $y$-smooth is $\ll\varrho(u)^{1+5/8-\varepsilon}$.
assumptions: For any $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $C > 0$ such that for any $x \ge 2$ and $y \in [(\log x)^C, x^{1/C}]$,

nodes.statement: For some applications, it would be interesting to obtain improved large sieve inequalities for sequences which display a mix of additive and multiplicative structure, such as \[ a_n := \sum_{\substack{h, h' \sim H \\ k, k' \sim K}} \mathbbm{1}_{hk\ell - h'k'\ell' = n}. \] In particular, this would be relevant for improving the total length in a mean-value estimate for the squared zeta function times a product of two Dirichlet polynomials, due to Deshouillers--Iwaniec \cite[Theorem 2]{deshouillers1984power} (and refined to an asymptotic by Bettin--Chandee--Radziwill \cite{bettin2017mean}). For an optimal choice of unbalanced ranges $M > N$, assuming Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture, one should reach the threshold $MN \le T^{5/8}$; the presence of the exponent $\tfrac{5}{8}$ here is not a coincidence, since these results rely on bounds for exponential sums of the shape in \cref{eq:sketch-kl-fractions}.

nodes.statement_short: Improved exceptional large sieve inequalities for sequences mixing additive and multiplicative structure would help mean values of $\zeta^2$ times Dirichlet polynomials.

nodes.statement: Although we will focus on equidistribution results with fixed (or small) residues $a$, similar results are possible in the range $a \ll x^{1+\varepsilon}$; this is relevant, e.g., to upper-bounding counts of Goldbach representations \cite{lichtman2023primes}. However, working with large values of $a$ ultimately has the effect of replacing some of the dependency on (progress towards) Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture with its non-Archimedean counterpart, the Ramanujan--Petersson conjecture at primes dividing $a$. In \cite{lichtman2023primes}, Lichtman incorporates technology of Assing--Blomer--Li \cite{assing2021uniform} to explicitate the dependency on the Ramanujan--Petersson conjecture; with this approach, the final exponent of distribution decreases with $a$. However, using appropriate non-Archimedean analogues of the large sieve inequalities \cite[Theorem 3]{pascadi2024large} and \cite[Theorem 2]{watt1995kloosterman}, one should be able to match the exponent of distribution $\tfrac{5}{8}-\varepsilon$ in a larger range of $a$, and in the full range $a \ll x^{1+\varepsilon}$ if $a$ is well-factorable.
nodes.name: Large residues and the Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture
nodes.statement_short: For large residues $a$ the dependence shifts to the Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture; non-Archimedean large sieves should recover exponent $5/8$.

nodes.statement: We write $\mathbb{Z}_+$ for the set of positive integers, $P^+(n)$ for the greatest prime factor of $n$, $(a, b) = \gcd(a, b)$, $[a, b] = \textnormal{lcm}(a, b)$, and $\overline{x}$ for the inverse of $x$ modulo $c$, where $c$ depends on the context.

nodes.statement: For $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$, we denote $\|\alpha\| := \min_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} |\alpha - n|$, which induces a norm on $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.statement: Following \cite[Notation 5]{pascadi2024large} (up to a constant), for $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ and $N > 0$ we use the notation \begin{equation} T_N(\alpha) := \min_{t \in \mathbb{Z}_+} \left(t + N\|t\alpha\|\right), \end{equation} which is nondecreasing in $N$, and measures the quality of rational approximations to $\alpha$ with small denominators $t$.
nodes.name: Rational approximation quality T_N
nodes.statement_short: $T_N(\alpha)=\min_t(t+N\|t\alpha\|)$ measures how well $\alpha$ is approximated by rationals with small denominators.

nodes.statement: We denote $e(\alpha) := e^{2\pi i \alpha}$ for $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$, and use the Fourier transform normalization \[ \widehat{f}(\xi) := \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(t) e(-\xi t) dt, \] for absolutely integrable functions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.name: Additive character and Fourier transform

nodes.statement: Let $x \gg 1$ and $1 \ll N, Q \ll x^{O(1)}$, $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, $q \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ with $q \asymp Q$, and $\Phi : (0, \infty) \to \mathbb{C}$ be a smooth function, $\Phi(t)$ supported in $t \asymp 1$, with $\Phi^{(k)} \ll_k 1$ for $k \ge 0$. Then for any $A, \delta > 0$ and $H := x^\delta N^{-1} Q$, one has \[ \begin{aligned} \sum_{n \equiv a \pmod{q}} \Phi\left(\frac{n}{N}\right) &= \frac{N}{q} \widehat{\Phi}(0) + O_{A,\delta}\left(x^{-A}\right) \\ &+ \frac{N}{Q} \int \Phi\left(\frac{uq}{Q}\right) \sum_{\substack{H_j = 2^j \\ 1 \le H_j \le H}} \sum_{h \in \mathbb{Z}} e\left(- h\frac{uN}{Q}\right) \Psi_j\left(\frac{|h|}{H_j}\right) e\left( \frac{ah}{q} \right) du, \end{aligned} \] where $\Psi_j : (\frac{1}{2}, 2) \to \mathbb{C}$ are some compactly supported functions with $\Psi_j^{(k)} \ll_k 1$ for $k \ge 0$. Note that the integrand is supported in $u \asymp 1$, and that one can rewrite \[ \frac{N}{Q} \Phi\left(\frac{uq}{Q}\right) du = \frac{N}{q} \widetilde\Phi\left(\frac{uq}{Q}\right) \frac{du}{u}, \qquad \text{where} \qquad \widetilde\Phi(t) := t\Phi(t). \]
nodes.name: Truncated Poisson with separation of variables
nodes.statement_short: Poisson summation for a smooth sum over $n\equiv a$ mod $q$, truncated to dual frequencies $|h|\le H$ with $h$ and $q$ separated.
assumptions: Let $x \gg 1$ and $1 \ll N, Q \ll x^{O(1)}$, $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, $q \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ with $q \asymp Q$, and $\Phi : (0, \infty) \to \mathbb{C}$ be a smooth function, $\Phi(t)$ supported in $t \asymp 1$, with $\Phi^{(k)} \ll_k 1$ for $k \ge 0$.
conclusions: Then for any $A, \delta > 0$ and $H := x^\delta N^{-1} Q$, one has \[ \begin{aligned} \sum_{n \equiv a \pmod{q}} \Phi\left(\frac{n}{N}\right) &= \frac{N}{q} \widehat{\Phi}(0) + O_{A,\delta}\left(x^{-A}\right) \\ &+ \frac{N}{Q} \int \Phi\left(\frac{uq}{Q}\right) \sum_{\substack{H_j = 2^j \\ 1 \le H_j \le H}} \sum_{h \in \mathbb{Z}} e\left(- h\frac{uN}{Q}\right) \Psi_j\left(\frac{|h|}{H_j}\right) e\left( \frac{ah}{q} \right) du, \end{aligned} \] where $\Psi_j : (\frac{1}{2}, 2) \to \mathbb{C}$ are some compactly supported functions with $\Psi_j^{(k)} \ll_k 1$ for $k \ge 0$. Note that the integrand is supported in $u \asymp 1$, and that one can rewrite \[ \frac{N}{Q} \Phi\left(\frac{uq}{Q}\right) du = \frac{N}{q} \widetilde\Phi\left(\frac{uq}{Q}\right) \frac{du}{u}, \qquad \text{where} \qquad \widetilde\Phi(t) := t\Phi(t). \]
nodes.label: lem:truncated-poisson

nodes.statement: This is \cite[Lemma 4]{pascadi2024large}, which follows quickly from the Poisson summation formula and a smooth dyadic partition of unity. Note that the variables $h$ and $q$ are separated at the cost of a slowly-varying exponential phase $e(h\omega)$ where $\omega = -uN/Q \ll x^\delta H^{-1}$.

nodes.statement: For a \emph{level} $q \in \mathbb{Z}_+$, we recall that $\Gamma_0(q)$ is the congruence subgroup of $\textnormal{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ consisting of all matrices with bottom-left entry divisible by $q$.
nodes.name: Congruence subgroup Gamma_0(q)
differentia: consisting of all matrices with bottom-left entry divisible by $q$
nodes.section: 3.2 Automorphic forms and large sieve inequalities

nodes.statement: The fundamental domain $\Gamma_0(q)\backslash \mathbb{H}$ has finitely many cusps, equivalent to fractions $u/w$ with $w \mid q$, $(u, w) = 1$, and $u \le (w, \tfrac{q}{w})$; in particular, the cusp at $\infty$ is equivalent to $1/q$.
nodes.name: Cusps of Gamma_0(q)
nodes.section: 3.2 Automorphic forms and large sieve inequalities
conclusions: The fundamental domain $\Gamma_0(q)\backslash \mathbb{H}$ has finitely many cusps, equivalent to fractions $u/w$ with $w \mid q$, $(u, w) = 1$, and $u \le (w, \tfrac{q}{w})$; in particular, the cusp at $\infty$ is equivalent to $1/q$.

nodes.statement: To a cusp $\mathfrak{a}$ we associate the parameter $\mu(\mathfrak{a}) := (w, \tfrac{q}{w})/q$, which will always equal $q^{-1}$ in this paper -- in other words, we will only use cusps equivalent to $1/s$ where $q = rs$, $(r, s) = 1$.
nodes.name: Cusp parameter mu

nodes.statement: For such a cusp $\mathfrak{a} = \tau(1/s)$, with $\tau \in \Gamma_0(q)$, we will use the choice of scaling matrix \begin{equation} \sigma_{\mathfrak{a}} := \tau \cdot \begin{pmatrix} \sqrt{r} & -\frac{\overline{s}}{\sqrt{r}} \\ s\sqrt{r} & \overline{r}\sqrt{r} \end{pmatrix}, \qquad\qquad \text{for some } \overline{r}, \overline{s} \in \mathbb{Z} \text{ with } r\overline{r} + s\overline{s} = 1, \end{equation} as in \cite[(3.9)]{pascadi2024large}; this matters in the Fourier-expansion of automorphic forms around $\mathfrak{a}$.

nodes.statement: As outlined in \cref{subsec:improvements}, the improvements in our final results come from the treatment of the exceptional spectrum, i.e., of the Maass cusp forms $f : \Gamma_0(q) \backslash \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ which are eigenforms of the hyperbolic Laplacian with eigenvalues $\lambda_f < 1/4$.
nodes.name: Exceptional spectrum
differentia: eigenforms of the hyperbolic Laplacian with eigenvalues $\lambda_f < 1/4$
nodes.section: 3.2 Automorphic forms and large sieve inequalities

nodes.statement: \cref{conj:selberg} predicts that there are no such eigenvalues, but unconditionally, they arise in the Kuznetsov trace formula \cite{deshouillers1982greatest,kuznetsov1980petersson} and its consequences through factors of $X^{\theta_f}$, where $\theta_f = \sqrt{1 - 4\lambda_f}$ and $X$ is typically large in applications; recall \cref{eq:before-di-cs}, where $X \approx \sqrt{x}$.
nodes.name: Spectral parameter theta_f

nodes.statement: Thus letting \[ \theta_{\max} := \sup_{q} \sup_f^{\Gamma_0(q)} \sqrt{\max(0, 1 - 4\lambda_f)}, \] Selberg's conjecture asserts that $\theta_{\max} = 0$, while the best (pointwise) unconditional result is due to Kim--Sarnak \cite[Appendix 2]{kim2003functoriality}: \begin{equation} \theta_{\max} \le \frac{7}{32}. \end{equation}

nodes.statement_short: $\theta_{\max}$ is the largest exceptional spectral parameter over all levels; Selberg predicts 0, Kim–Sarnak give $7/32$.

nodes.statement: \theta_{\max} \le \frac{7}{32}.

nodes.statement: We say that a tuple $(q, N, Z, (a_n)_{n \sim N}, A, Y)$, with $q \in \mathbb{Z}_+$, $N \ge 1/2$, $Z \gg 1$, $A \gg \|a_n\|_2$, $Y > 0$, satisfies this assumption iff the following holds. For any $\varepsilon > 0$, $\xi \in \mathbb{R}$, any cusp $\mathfrak{a}$ of $\Gamma_0(q)$ with $\mu(\mathfrak{a}) = q^{-1}$, and any orthonormal basis of exceptional Maass cusp forms $f$ for $\Gamma_0(q)$, with Laplacian eigenvalues $\lambda_f$, $\theta_f := \sqrt{1-4\lambda_f}$, and Fourier coefficients $\rho_{f\mathfrak{a}}(n)$ (using the choice of scaling matrix in \cref{eq:scaling-choices}), one has \[ \sum_{\substack{f \\ \lambda_f < 1/4}}^{\Gamma_0(q)} X^{\theta_f} \left\vert \sum_{n \sim N} e\left(\frac{n}{N} \xi \right) a_n\, \rho_{f\mathfrak{a}}(n) \right\vert^2 \ll_\varepsilon (qNZ)^\varepsilon \left(1 + \frac{N}{q}\right) A^2, \] for all \begin{equation} X \ll \max\left(1, \frac{q}{N}\right) \frac{Y}{1+|\xi|^2}. \end{equation}

nodes.statement: Let $N \ge 1/2$, $L, H \gg 1$, $\alpha_1, \alpha_2 \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$, and $q, \ell_1, \ell_2 \in \mathbb{Z}_+$, $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ be such that $q \gg L^2$, $\ell_1, \ell_2 \asymp L$, and $(\ell_1, \ell_2) = 1$. Let $\Phi_i(t) : (0, \infty) \to \mathbb{C}$ be smooth functions supported in $t \ll 1$, with $\Phi_i^{(j)} \ll_j 1$ for all $j \ge 0$, and \[ a_n := \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \in \mathbb{Z} \\ a(h_1 \ell_1 - h_2 \ell_2) = n}} \Phi_1\left(\frac{h_1}{H}\right) \Phi_2\left(\frac{h_2}{H}\right) e(h_1 \alpha_1 + h_2 \alpha_2). \] Then the tuple $(q, N, H, (a_n)_{n \sim N}, A, Y)$ satisfies \cref{ass:large-sieve}, where \[ A := \|a_n\|_2 + \sqrt{N \left(\frac{H}{L} + \frac{H^2}{L^2}\right)}, \qquad\qquad Y := \max\left(1, \frac{NH}{|a|(H+L)L\min_i T_H(\alpha_i)}\right). \]
nodes.name: Large sieve with additive convolutions
nodes.statement_short: Sequences given by additive convolutions $a(h_1\ell_1-h_2\ell_2)=n$ of smooth sequences satisfy the large sieve assumption with an extra saving $Y$.

assumptions: Let $N \ge 1/2$, $L, H \gg 1$, $\alpha_1, \alpha_2 \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$, and $q, \ell_1, \ell_2 \in \mathbb{Z}_+$, $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ be such that $q \gg L^2$, $\ell_1, \ell_2 \asymp L$, and $(\ell_1, \ell_2) = 1$. Let $\Phi_i(t) : (0, \infty) \to \mathbb{C}$ be smooth functions supported in $t \ll 1$, with $\Phi_i^{(j)} \ll_j 1$ for all $j \ge 0$, and \[ a_n := \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \in \mathbb{Z} \\ a(h_1 \ell_1 - h_2 \ell_2) = n}} \Phi_1\left(\frac{h_1}{H}\right) \Phi_2\left(\frac{h_2}{H}\right) e(h_1 \alpha_1 + h_2 \alpha_2). \]
conclusions: Then the tuple $(q, N, H, (a_n)_{n \sim N}, A, Y)$ satisfies \cref{ass:large-sieve}, where \[ A := \|a_n\|_2 + \sqrt{N \left(\frac{H}{L} + \frac{H^2}{L^2}\right)}, \qquad\qquad Y := \max\left(1, \frac{NH}{|a|(H+L)L\min_i T_H(\alpha_i)}\right). \]

nodes.statement: This follows from \cite[Theorem 3]{pascadi2024large} with $a_n \gets a_{n/|a|}$, $N \gets N/|a|$, $a \gets |a|$, as in \cite[(5.18)]{pascadi2024large} (we note that the statement is trivial unless $N \ll |a|HL$, and recall our notation \cref{eq:tn}). One can in fact replace $T_H(\alpha_i)$ with the smaller quantity $T_{N/(|a|L)}(\alpha_i)$ (up to a constant), which is helpful in incorporating the phase $\xi$ from \cref{ass:large-sieve} via the bound \[ T_{N/(|a|L)}\left(\alpha_i \pm \frac{a\ell_i \xi}{N} \right) \ll \left(1 + \frac{N}{|a|L} \frac{|a \ell_i \xi|}{N}\right) T_{N/(|a|L)}(\alpha_i) \ll (1 + |\xi|) T_H(\alpha_i). \]

nodes.statement: Let $\varepsilon$, $X > 0$, $Q \ge 1/2$, $N_1, N_2, Z \gg 1$, and $\Psi_1(t), \Psi_2(t)$ be smooth functions supported $t \asymp 1$, with $\Phi_i^{(j)} \ll_j Z^j$ for $j \ge 0$. Let $q \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ and $\infty_q$ be the cusp at $\infty$ of $\Gamma_0(q)$. Then using the same notation as in \cref{ass:large-sieve}, \[ \sum_{q \sim Q} \sum_{\substack{f \\ \lambda_f < 1/4}}^{\Gamma_0(q)} X^{\theta_f} \left\vert \sum_{n_1, n_2} \Psi_1\left(\frac{n_1}{N_1}\right) \Psi_2\left(\frac{n_2}{N_2}\right) \rho_{f\infty_q}(n_1 n_2) \right\vert^2 \ll_\varepsilon Q^\varepsilon Z^5 \left(Q + N_1 N_2\right) N_1 N_2 \] holds for any \begin{equation} X \ll \frac{Q^2}{N_1^2 N_2}. \end{equation}

nodes.statement: We recall the classical Kloosterman sums, given for $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $c \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ by \[ S(m, n; c) := \sum_{x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^\times} e\left(\frac{mx + n\overline{x}}{c}\right), \] where $x\overline{x} \equiv 1 \pmod{c}$.
nodes.name: Kloosterman sum

nodes.statement: For any $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $c \in \mathbb{Z}_+$, \[ \begin{aligned} S(m, n; c) &\ll \tau(c)\, (m, n, c)^{1/2} c^{1/2}, \\ |S(0, n; c)| &\le (n, c). \end{aligned} \]
nodes.name: Weil and Ramanujan bounds
assumptions: For any $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $c \in \mathbb{Z}_+$
conclusions: \[ \begin{aligned} S(m, n; c) &\ll \tau(c)\, (m, n, c)^{1/2} c^{1/2}, \\ |S(0, n; c)| &\le (n, c). \end{aligned} \]

nodes.statement: The first bound is due to Weil, and uses algebraic geometry; see \cite[Corollary 11.12]{iwaniec2021analytic}. The second bound is classical and follows from M\"obius inversion.

nodes.statement: Let $R, S, N \ge 1/2$, $C, D, Z \gg 1$, and $Y, \varepsilon > 0$. For all $r \sim R$, $s \sim S$ with $(r, s) = 1$, let: \begin{itemize} \item $w_{r,s} \in \mathbb{C}$; \item $\Phi_{r,s} : (0, \infty)^3 \to \mathbb{C}$ be smooth, with $\Phi_{r,s}(x, y, z)$ supported in $x, y, z \asymp 1$, and \[ \partial_x^j \partial_y^k \partial_z^\ell \Phi_q(x, y, z) \ll_{j,k,\ell,\varepsilon} Z^{j\varepsilon}, \qquad \forall j, k, \ell \ge 0; \] \item $(rs, N, Z, (a_{n,r,s})_{n \sim N}, A_{r,s}, Y)$ be a tuple satisfying \cref{ass:large-sieve}. \end{itemize} Then with a consistent choice of the sign $\pm$, it holds that \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{r \sim R \\ s \sim S \\ (r, s) = 1}} w_{r,s} \sum_{n \sim N} a_{n,r,s} \sum_{\substack{c, d \\ (rd, sc) = 1}} \Phi_{r,s}\left(\frac{n}{N}, \frac{d}{D}, \frac{c}{C}\right) e\left(\pm n \frac{\overline{rd}}{sc}\right) \ll_\varepsilon (RSNCDZ)^{O(\varepsilon)}\, \|w_{r,s} A_{r,s}\|_2 \mathscr{I}, \end{equation} where \[ \mathscr{I}^2 := D^2 NR + \left(1 + \frac{C^2}{R^2 S Y}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} CS(C + DR)(RS + N). \]

nodes.statement_short: Bound for multilinear sums of incomplete Kloosterman fractions whose $n$-coefficients satisfy the exceptional large sieve assumption.
assumptions: Let $R, S, N \ge 1/2$, $C, D, Z \gg 1$, and $Y, \varepsilon > 0$. conclusions: Then with a consistent choice of the sign $\pm$, it holds that \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{r \sim R \\ s \sim S \\ (r, s) = 1}} w_{r,s} \sum_{n \sim N} a_{n,r,s} \sum_{\substack{c, d \\ (rd, sc) = 1}} \Phi_{r,s}\left(\frac{n}{N}, \frac{d}{D}, \frac{c}{C}\right) e\left(\pm n \frac{\overline{rd}}{sc}\right) \ll_\varepsilon (RSNCDZ)^{O(\varepsilon)}\, \|w_{r,s} A_{r,s}\|_2 \mathscr{I}, \end{equation} where \[ \mathscr{I}^2 := D^2 NR + \left(1 + \frac{C^2}{R^2 S Y}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} CS(C + DR)(RS + N). \]
nodes.label: prop:kloosterman-incomplete

nodes.statement: Let $R, S, N \ge 1/2$, $M_1, M_2, C, Z \gg 1$, $M \asymp M_1 M_2$, and $Y, \varepsilon > 0$. For all $r \sim R$, $s \sim S$ with $(r, s) = 1$, let: \begin{itemize} \item $w_{r,s} \in \mathbb{C}$; \item $\Phi_{r,s} : (0, \infty)^4 \to \mathbb{C}$ be smooth, with $\Phi_{r,s}(x_1, x_2, y, z)$ supported in $x_1, x_2, y, z \asymp 1$, and \[ \partial_{x_1}^{j_1} \partial_{x_2}^{j_2} \partial_y^k \partial_z^\ell \Phi_q(x_1, x_2, y, z) \ll_{j_1,j_2,k,\ell,\varepsilon} Z^{(j_1+j_2+k)\varepsilon}, \qquad \forall j_1, j_2, k, \ell \ge 0; \] \item $(rs, N, Z, (a_{n,r,s})_{n \sim N}, A_{r,s}, Y)$ be a tuple satisfying \cref{ass:large-sieve}. \end{itemize} Then with a consistent choice of the sign $\pm$, it holds that \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \sum_{\substack{r \sim R \\ s \sim S \\ (r, s) = 1}} w_{r,s} \sum_{m_1, m_2 \in \mathbb{Z}} \sum_{n \sim N} a_{n,r,s} \sum_{(c, r) = 1} \Phi_{r,s}\left(\frac{m_1}{M_1}, \frac{m_2}{M_2}, \frac{n}{N}, \frac{c}{C}\right) S(m_1m_2\overline{r}, \pm n; sc) \ll_\varepsilon (RSMNCZ)^{O(\varepsilon)} \\ \times \left(1 + \frac{C \sqrt{M_1}}{R \sqrt{SY}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \|w_{r,s} A_{r,s}\|_2 \sqrt{RSM} \left(\frac{C^2}{R} (M + RS)(N + RS) + MN \right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.name: Sums of Kloosterman sums with multiplicative convolutions
nodes.statement_short: Bound for sums of Kloosterman sums $S(m_1m_2\bar r,\pm n;sc)$ where the $m$-coefficient is a product of two smooth sequences, using Watt's large sieve.
assumptions: Let $R, S, N \ge 1/2$, $M_1, M_2, C, Z \gg 1$, $M \asymp M_1 M_2$, and $Y, \varepsilon > 0$. For all $r \sim R$, $s \sim S$ with $(r, s) = 1$, let: \begin{itemize} \item $w_{r,s} \in \mathbb{C}$; \item $\Phi_{r,s} : (0, \infty)^4 \to \mathbb{C}$ be smooth, with $\Phi_{r,s}(x_1, x_2, y, z)$ supported in $x_1, x_2, y, z \asymp 1$, and \[ \partial_{x_1}^{j_1} \partial_{x_2}^{j_2} \partial_y^k \partial_z^\ell \Phi_q(x_1, x_2, y, z) \ll_{j_1,j_2,k,\ell,\varepsilon} Z^{(j_1+j_2+k)\varepsilon}, \qquad \forall j_1, j_2, k, \ell \ge 0; \] \item $(rs, N, Z, (a_{n,r,s})_{n \sim N}, A_{r,s}, Y)$ be a tuple satisfying \cref{ass:large-sieve}. \end{itemize}
conclusions: Then with a consistent choice of the sign $\pm$, it holds that \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \sum_{\substack{r \sim R \\ s \sim S \\ (r, s) = 1}} w_{r,s} \sum_{m_1, m_2 \in \mathbb{Z}} \sum_{n \sim N} a_{n,r,s} \sum_{(c, r) = 1} \Phi_{r,s}\left(\frac{m_1}{M_1}, \frac{m_2}{M_2}, \frac{n}{N}, \frac{c}{C}\right) S(m_1m_2\overline{r}, \pm n; sc) \ll_\varepsilon (RSMNCZ)^{O(\varepsilon)} \\ \times \left(1 + \frac{C \sqrt{M_1}}{R \sqrt{SY}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \|w_{r,s} A_{r,s}\|_2 \sqrt{RSM} \left(\frac{C^2}{R} (M + RS)(N + RS) + MN \right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \end{equation}

nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \sum_{\substack{r \sim R \\ s \sim S \\ (r, s) = 1}} w_{r,s} \sum_{m_1, m_2 \in \mathbb{Z}} \sum_{n \sim N} a_{n,r,s} \sum_{(c, r) = 1} \Phi_{r,s}\left(\frac{m_1}{M_1}, \frac{m_2}{M_2}, \frac{n}{N}, \frac{c}{C}\right) S(m_1m_2\overline{r}, \pm n; sc) \ll_\varepsilon (RSMNCZ)^{O(\varepsilon)} \\ \times \left(1 + \frac{C \sqrt{M_1}}{R \sqrt{SY}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \|w_{r,s} A_{r,s}\|_2 \sqrt{RSM} \left(\frac{C^2}{R} (M + RS)(N + RS) + MN \right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned}

nodes.statement: We closely follow the proof of \cite[Corollary 17]{pascadi2023smooth}, with minor changes. We start by inserting coefficients $\Psi_i(m_i/M_i)$ in the sum $\mathcal{S}$ from the left-hand side of \cref{eq:kloosterman-rsm12nc}; here $\Psi_i(t)$ are smooth functions with $\Psi_i^{(j)} \ll_j 1$, supported in $t \asymp 1$, and equal to $1$ on the supports of $x_1, x_2 \asymp 1$ in $\Phi_{r,s}(x_1, x_2, y, z)$. We then separate variables using the Fourier inversion formula \[ \begin{aligned} \Psi_{r,s}(x_1, x_2, y; z) &:= \sqrt{x_1 x_2 y}\,\Phi_{r,s}\left(x_1, x_2, y, \frac{\sqrt{x_1 x_2 y}}{z} \right) \\ &= \iiint_{\mathbb{R}^3} \widehat{\Psi}_{r,s}(\zeta_1, \zeta_2, \xi; z) \, e(x_1\zeta_1 + x_2\zeta_2 + y\xi)\, d\zeta_1\, d\zeta_2\, d\xi, \end{aligned} \] where the Fourier transform is taken in the first three variables. Thus \[ \begin{aligned} \Phi_{r,s}\left(\frac{m_1}{M_1}, \frac{m_2}{M_2}, \frac{n}{N}, \frac{c}{C}\right) &= \frac{\sqrt{M_1M_2N}}{\sqrt{m_1m_2n}} \\ &\times \iiint_{\mathbb{R}^2} \widehat{\Psi}_{r,s}\left(\zeta_1, \zeta_2, \xi; \frac{C\sqrt{m_1m_2n}}{c\sqrt{M_1M_2N}}\right) \, e\left(\frac{m_1}{M_1}\zeta_1 + \frac{m_2}{M_2}\zeta_2 + \frac{n}{N}\xi\right)\, d\zeta_1\, d\zeta_2\, d\xi. \end{aligned} \] Similarly as in \cite[(5.21)]{pascadi2024large}, this yields \begin{equation} \mathcal{S} \ll_\varepsilon Z^{O(\varepsilon)} CS\sqrt{R} \iiint_{\mathbb{R}^2} \frac{S(\zeta_1, \zeta_2, \xi)\, d\zeta_1\, d\zeta_2\, d\xi}{(1 + \zeta_1^{100}) (1 + \zeta_2^{100}) (1 + \xi^{100})}, \end{equation} where \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{S}(\zeta_1, \zeta_2, \xi) := \sum_{\substack{r \sim R \\ s \sim S \\ (r, s) = 1}} |w_{r,s}| \Bigg\vert \sum_{m_1, m_2 \in \mathbb{Z}} \Psi_1\left(\frac{m_1}{M_1}\right) \Psi_2\left(\frac{m_2}{M_2}\right) e\left(\frac{m_1}{M_1}\zeta_1 + \frac{m_2}{M_2}\zeta_2\right) \sum_{n \sim N} b_n\, e\left(\frac{n}{N}\xi\right) \\ \times \sum_{(c, r) = 1}\, \frac{S(m_1 m_2 \overline{r}, \pm n; sc)}{cs\sqrt{r}} \varphi_{\zeta_1,\zeta_2,\xi,r,s}\left(\frac{4\pi \sqrt{m_1 m_2 n}}{c}\right) \Bigg\vert, \end{aligned} \] and $\varphi_{\zeta_1, \zeta_2, \xi, r, s}(z)$ is supported in $z \asymp X^{-1}$, and satisfies $\varphi_{\zeta_1,\zeta_2,\xi}^{(\ell)} \ll_\ell X^\ell$ for \begin{equation} X := \frac{CS\sqrt{R}}{\sqrt{MN}}. \end{equation} We can incorporate the factors $e(t \zeta_i)$ into the functions $\Psi_i(t)$, incurring derivative bounds $\Psi_i^{(j)} \ll_j 1 + |\zeta_i|^j$. From here on, the proof is analogous to that of \cite[Corollary 17]{pascadi2024large} (starting with an application of the Kuznetsov formula for the cusps $\infty$ and $1/s$), except that we apply \cref{prop:large-sieve-multiplicative} instead of \cite[Theorem J]{pascadi2024large} in the exceptional spectrum; we use $Z = \max_i(1 + |\zeta_i|)$ in \cref{prop:large-sieve-multiplicative}, which disappears in the integral over $\zeta_1, \zeta_2$ from \cref{eq:final-kloosterman-integral}. Importantly, instead of \cite[(5.33)]{pascadi2023smooth} we use \[ X_1 := \frac{Q^2}{M_1^2 M_2}, \] as in \cref{eq:watt-saving}. Combining this with the value of $X$ from \cref{eq:initial-X-factor} and the value of $X_2(\xi)$ from \cref{eq:x-saving-ass} (with $q = rs$) leads to a total exceptional factor of \[ \begin{aligned} \left(1 + \frac{X}{\sqrt{X_1 X_2(0)}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} &\ll \left(1 + \frac{CS\sqrt{R}}{\sqrt{M_1 M_2 N}} \frac{M_1 \sqrt{M_2}}{Q} \frac{\sqrt{N}}{\sqrt{RSY}} \right)^{\theta_{\max}} \\ &= \left(1 + \frac{C\sqrt{M_1}}{R\sqrt{SY}} \right)^{\theta_{\max}} , \end{aligned} \] as in \cref{eq:kloosterman-rsm12nc}. Other than this, the right-hand side of \cref{eq:kloosterman-rsm12nc} is identical to that of \cite[(5.31)]{pascadi2024large}, after inserting the follow-up bound from \cite[(5.32)]{pascadi2024large}.
nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.8
nodes.statement_short: Follow Pascadi's Corollary 17: separate variables by Fourier inversion, apply Kuznetsov, and use Watt's large sieve in the exceptional spectrum. The key change is the exceptional factor $X_1=Q^2/(M_1^2M_2)$.

nodes.name: Reduce to integral of sums
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\mathcal S$ by an integral of Kloosterman-sum averages with a Bessel-type weight at scale $X$.

nodes.statement: \mathcal{S} \ll_\varepsilon Z^{O(\varepsilon)} CS\sqrt{R} \iiint_{\mathbb{R}^2} \frac{S(\zeta_1, \zeta_2, \xi)\, d\zeta_1\, d\zeta_2\, d\xi}{(1 + \zeta_1^{100}) (1 + \zeta_2^{100}) (1 + \xi^{100})},
nodes.name: Equation (3.8) eq:final-kloosterman-integral
nodes.label: eq:final-kloosterman-integral

nodes.statement: X := \frac{CS\sqrt{R}}{\sqrt{MN}}.
nodes.name: Equation (3.9) eq:initial-X-factor
nodes.label: eq:initial-X-factor

nodes.statement: We can incorporate the factors $e(t \zeta_i)$ into the functions $\Psi_i(t)$, incurring derivative bounds $\Psi_i^{(j)} \ll_j 1 + |\zeta_i|^j$. From here on, the proof is analogous to that of \cite[Corollary 17]{pascadi2024large} (starting with an application of the Kuznetsov formula for the cusps $\infty$ and $1/s$), except that we apply \cref{prop:large-sieve-multiplicative} instead of \cite[Theorem J]{pascadi2024large} in the exceptional spectrum; we use $Z = \max_i(1 + |\zeta_i|)$ in \cref{prop:large-sieve-multiplicative}, which disappears in the integral over $\zeta_1, \zeta_2$ from \cref{eq:final-kloosterman-integral}.
nodes.name: Kuznetsov and Watt's large sieve
nodes.statement_short: Apply Kuznetsov and use Watt's large sieve (Prop. 3.5) in the exceptional spectrum.

nodes.statement: Importantly, instead of \cite[(5.33)]{pascadi2023smooth} we use \[ X_1 := \frac{Q^2}{M_1^2 M_2}, \] as in \cref{eq:watt-saving}. Combining this with the value of $X$ from \cref{eq:initial-X-factor} and the value of $X_2(\xi)$ from \cref{eq:x-saving-ass} (with $q = rs$) leads to a total exceptional factor of \[ \begin{aligned} \left(1 + \frac{X}{\sqrt{X_1 X_2(0)}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} &\ll \left(1 + \frac{CS\sqrt{R}}{\sqrt{M_1 M_2 N}} \frac{M_1 \sqrt{M_2}}{Q} \frac{\sqrt{N}}{\sqrt{RSY}} \right)^{\theta_{\max}} \\ &= \left(1 + \frac{C\sqrt{M_1}}{R\sqrt{SY}} \right)^{\theta_{\max}} , \end{aligned} \] as in \cref{eq:kloosterman-rsm12nc}.
nodes.name: Exceptional factor
nodes.statement_short: Combine $X$, $X_1$ and $X_2$ into the exceptional factor of (3.7).

nodes.statement: Other than this, the right-hand side of \cref{eq:kloosterman-rsm12nc} is identical to that of \cite[(5.31)]{pascadi2024large}, after inserting the follow-up bound from \cite[(5.32)]{pascadi2024large}.
nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement_short: The rest matches Pascadi's (5.31)–(5.32).

nodes.statement: Let $\varepsilon > 0$, $a \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, $1 \ll S, F, K, C, H \ll x^{O(1)}$, $\Phi_i(t)$ be smooth functions supported in $t \asymp 1$ with $\Phi_i^{(j)} \ll_j 1$, and \[ \phi(h_1, h_2) := \Phi_1\left(\frac{h_1}{H}\right) \Phi_2\left(\frac{h_2}{H}\right) e(h_1\alpha_1 + h_2\alpha_2), \] where $\alpha_i \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ have $\min_i T_H(\alpha_i) \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon$ (recall \cref{eq:tn}). Then for any smooth function $\Phi(x_1, x_2, z)$ supported in $x_i, z \asymp 1$, satisfying $\partial_{x_1}^{j_1} \partial_{x_2}^{j_2} \partial_z^\ell \Phi(x_1, x_2, z) \ll_{j_1, j_2, \ell, \varepsilon} x^{(j_1+j_2) \varepsilon}$, one has \[ \begin{aligned} &\sum_{s_1, s_2 \sim S} \left\vert \sum_{f,k} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \\ \ell = h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2 \neq 0}} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{(c, s_1s_2) = 1} \Phi\left(\frac{f}{F}, \frac{k}{K}, \frac{c}{C}\right) S(fk\overline{s_1 s_2}, a\ell; c) \right\vert \\ &\ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{O(\varepsilon)} \left(1 + \frac{C\sqrt{F}}{S^2\sqrt{\frac{H^2}{H+S}}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \sqrt{H^2S^3 (H + S) F K} \left(\frac{C^2}{S}\left(FK + S^2\right)\left(H + S\right) + FKHS\right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \]
nodes.name: Consequence of the Kloosterman bounds for additive sequences
nodes.statement_short: Bound for a sum over $s_1,s_2$ of Kloosterman sums $S(fk\overline{s_1s_2},a\ell;c)$ with $\ell=h_1s_1-h_2s_2$, from the additive and multiplicative large sieves.
assumptions: Let $\varepsilon > 0$, $a \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, $1 \ll S, F, K, C, H \ll x^{O(1)}$, $\Phi_i(t)$ be smooth functions supported in $t \asymp 1$ with $\Phi_i^{(j)} \ll_j 1$, and \[ \phi(h_1, h_2) := \Phi_1\left(\frac{h_1}{H}\right) \Phi_2\left(\frac{h_2}{H}\right) e(h_1\alpha_1 + h_2\alpha_2), \] where $\alpha_i \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ have $\min_i T_H(\alpha_i) \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon$ (recall \cref{eq:tn}).
conclusions: Then for any smooth function $\Phi(x_1, x_2, z)$ supported in $x_i, z \asymp 1$, satisfying $\partial_{x_1}^{j_1} \partial_{x_2}^{j_2} \partial_z^\ell \Phi(x_1, x_2, z) \ll_{j_1, j_2, \ell, \varepsilon} x^{(j_1+j_2) \varepsilon}$, one has \[ \begin{aligned} &\sum_{s_1, s_2 \sim S} \left\vert \sum_{f,k} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \\ \ell = h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2 \neq 0}} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{(c, s_1s_2) = 1} \Phi\left(\frac{f}{F}, \frac{k}{K}, \frac{c}{C}\right) S(fk\overline{s_1 s_2}, a\ell; c) \right\vert \\ &\ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{O(\varepsilon)} \left(1 + \frac{C\sqrt{F}}{S^2\sqrt{\frac{H^2}{H+S}}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \sqrt{H^2S^3 (H + S) F K} \left(\frac{C^2}{S}\left(FK + S^2\right)\left(H + S\right) + FKHS\right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \]
nodes.label: lem:consequence-Kloosterman

nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{K}_0$ denote the sum in the left-hand side. We first let $s_0 := (s_1, s_2)$, change variables $s_i \gets s_0 s_i$, $\ell \gets s_0 \ell$ for $i \in \{1, 2\}$, and put $s_0$ into dyadic ranges. This yields \begin{equation} \mathcal{K}_0 \ll x^{o(1)} \sup_{S_0 \ll S} \mathcal{K}_1(S_0), \end{equation} where after simplifying $S(fk\overline{s_0^2 s_1 s_2}, a s_0 \ell; c) = S(fk\overline{s_0 s_1 s_2}, a\ell; c)$, \[ \mathcal{K}_1 := \sum_{s_0 \sim S_0} \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S/s_0 \\ (s_1, s_2) = 1}} \Bigg\vert \sum_{f,k} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \\ \ell = h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2 \neq 0}} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{(c, s_0 s_1 s_2) = 1} \Phi\left(\frac{f}{F}, \frac{k}{K}, \frac{c}{C}\right) S(fk\overline{s_0 s_1 s_2}, a\ell; c) \Bigg\vert. \] We then put $n = |a\ell|$ and $r = s_0 s_1 s_2$ in dyadic ranges $n \sim \mathcal{N}$, $r \sim \mathcal{R}$, insert coefficients $\Psi(n/\mathcal{N})$ where $\Psi^{(j)} \ll_j 1$ and $\psi \equiv 1$ on $[1, 2]$, and use the divisor bound to write \begin{equation} \mathcal{K}_1 \ll x^{o(1)} \sup_{\substack{\mathcal{N} \ll_a HS/S_0 \\ \mathcal{R} \asymp S^2 / S_0}} \mathcal{K}_2(\mathcal{N}, \mathcal{R}), \end{equation} for \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathcal{K}_2 := \sum_{r \sim \mathcal{R}} \max_{\substack{s_0 \sim S_0 \\ s_1, s_2 \sim S/s_0 \\ (s_1, s_2) = 1 \\ s_0 s_1 s_2 = r}} \Bigg\vert \sum_{f,k} \sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \\ a(h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2) = \pm n}} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{(c, r) = 1} \Psi\left(\frac{n}{\mathcal{N}}\right) \Phi\left(\frac{f}{F}, \frac{k}{K}, \frac{c}{C} \right) S(fk\overline{r}, \pm n; c) \Bigg\vert, \end{aligned} \end{equation} where the supremum in \cref{eq:K1-split} includes the choice of the $\pm$ sign. If the maximum above is attained at some $s_1(r), s_2(r)$, we let \[ a_{n,r} := \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \in \mathbb{Z} \\ a(h_1 s_1(r) - h_2 s_2(r)) = \pm n}} \phi(h_1, h_2) = \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \in \mathbb{Z} \\ \pm a(h_1 s_1(r) - h_2 s_2(r)) = n}} \Phi_1\left(\frac{h_1}{H}\right) \Phi_2\left(\frac{h_2}{H}\right) e(h_1\alpha_1 + h_2\alpha_2). \] If the maximum is empty, we let $a_{n, r} := 0$. Then we can rewrite \cref{eq:K2} as \[ \mathcal{K}_2 = \sum_{r \sim \mathcal{R}} \Bigg\vert \sum_{f,k} \sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} a_{n,r} \sum_{(c, r) = 1} \Psi\left(\frac{n}{\mathcal{N}}\right) \Phi\left(\frac{f}{F}, \frac{k}{K}, \frac{c}{C} \right) S(fk\overline{r}, \pm n; c) \Bigg\vert. \] By \cref{prop:large-sieve-additive}, the tuple $(r, \mathcal{N}, x, (a_{n,r})_{n \sim \mathcal{N}}, A_r, Y)$ satisfies \cref{ass:large-sieve}, where \[ Y := \frac{\mathcal{N} H}{|a|(H+S/S_0)(S/S_0) \min_i T_H(\alpha_i)}, \qquad A_r := \left(\sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} |a_{n,r}|^2\right)^{1/2} + \sqrt{\mathcal{N}} \sqrt{\frac{H S_0}{S} + \frac{H^2 S_0^2}{S^2}}. \] Since $\min_i T_H(\alpha_i) \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon$, we further have \[ Y \gg_{\varepsilon,a} x^{-\varepsilon}\frac{\mathcal{N} H S_0}{(H+S)S}. \] We can now apply \cref{prop:kloosterman-complete}; specifically, by \cref{eq:kloosterman-rsm12nc}, we obtain \[ \mathcal{K}_2 \ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{O(\varepsilon)} \left(1 + \frac{C\sqrt{F}}{\mathcal{R}\sqrt{\frac{\mathcal{N} H S_0}{(H+S)S}}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \|A_r\|_2 \sqrt{\mathcal{R} F K} \left(\frac{C^2}{\mathcal{R}}(FK + \mathcal{R})(\mathcal{N} + \mathcal{R}) + FK\mathcal{N}\right)^{1/2}. \] We claim that \begin{equation} \|A_r\|_2^2 \ll x^{o(1)} \mathcal{N}(HS + H^2 S_0). \end{equation} Indeed, this follows from the definition of $A_r$ and the two bounds \[ \sum_{r \sim \mathcal{R}} \mathcal{N} \left(\frac{HS_0}{S} + \frac{H^2 S_0^2}{S^2}\right) \asymp \frac{S^2}{S_0} \mathcal{N} \left(\frac{HS_0}{S} + \frac{H^2 S_0^2}{S^2}\right) \asymp \mathcal{N} (HS + H^2 S_0), \] \[ \begin{aligned} \sum_{r \sim \mathcal{R}} \sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} |a_{n,r}|^2 &\ll \sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} \sum_{s_0 \sim S_0} \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S/s_0 \\ (s_1, s_2) = 1}} \left( \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \asymp H \\ h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2 = \pm n/a}} 1 \right)^2 \\ &\ll \sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} \sum_{s_0 \sim S_0} \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S/s_0 \\ (s_1, s_2) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \asymp H \\ h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2 = \pm n/a}}\, \sum_{\substack{h_1', h_2' \asymp H \\ s_1(h_1 - h_1') = s_2(h_2 - h_2')}} 1 \\ &\ll \sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} \sum_{s_0 \sim S_0} \sum_{\substack{s_1 \sim S/s_0 \\ h_1 \asymp H}} \sum_{\substack{s_2 \sim S/s_0 \\ h_2 \asymp H \\ h_2 s_2 = h_1 s_1 \mp n/a}} \sum_{\substack{h_1' \asymp H \\ h_1' \equiv h_1 \pmod{s_2}}}\, \sum_{\substack{h_2' \asymp H \\ s_1(h_1 - h_1') = s_2(h_2 - h_2')}} 1 \\ &\ll x^{o(1)} \mathcal{N} S_0 \frac{S}{S_0} H \left(1 + \frac{H S_0}{S}\right) \quad = x^{o(1)} \mathcal{N} (HS + H^2 S_0). \end{aligned} \] Using \cref{eq:primes-l2-bound}, we can further bound \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{K}_2 &\ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{O(\varepsilon)} \\ &\times \left(1 + \frac{C\sqrt{F}}{\mathcal{R}\sqrt{\frac{\mathcal{N} H S_0}{(H+S)S}}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \sqrt{\mathcal{N} (HS + H^2 S_0) \mathcal{R} F K} \left(\frac{C^2}{\mathcal{R}}(FK + \mathcal{R})(\mathcal{N} + \mathcal{R}) + FK\mathcal{N}\right)^{1/2}, \end{aligned} \] where the right-hand side is increasing in $\mathcal{N} \ll_a HS/S_0$. Substituting this value of $\mathcal{N}$ and $\mathcal{R} \asymp S^2/S_0$, it follows from \cref{eq:K1-split} that \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{K}_1 &\ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{O(\varepsilon)} \left(1 + \frac{C\sqrt{F}}{\frac{S^2}{S_0}\sqrt{\frac{H^2}{H+S}}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \\ &\times \sqrt{\frac{HS}{S_0} (HS + H^2 S_0) \frac{S^2}{S_0} F K} \left(\frac{C^2 S_0}{S^2}\left(FK + \frac{S^2}{S_0}\right)\left(\frac{HS}{S_0} + \frac{S^2}{S_0}\right) + \frac{FKHS}{S_0}\right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \] Since $\theta_{\max} < 1/2$, the right-hand side is seen to be decreasing in $S_0 \gg 1$; substituting $S_0$ with $1$ and plugging this into \cref{eq:K-split}, we obtain the desired bound for $\mathcal{K}_0$.
nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement_short: Extract $\gcd(s_1,s_2)$, split dyadically, then combine the additive large sieve with the multiplicative-convolution Kloosterman bound. Key step: the $\ell^2$ bound (4.4) for $A_r$.

nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{K}_0$ denote the sum in the left-hand side. We first let $s_0 := (s_1, s_2)$, change variables $s_i \gets s_0 s_i$, $\ell \gets s_0 \ell$ for $i \in \{1, 2\}$, and put $s_0$ into dyadic ranges. This yields \begin{equation} \mathcal{K}_0 \ll x^{o(1)} \sup_{S_0 \ll S} \mathcal{K}_1(S_0), \end{equation} where after simplifying $S(fk\overline{s_0^2 s_1 s_2}, a s_0 \ell; c) = S(fk\overline{s_0 s_1 s_2}, a\ell; c)$, \[ \mathcal{K}_1 := \sum_{s_0 \sim S_0} \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S/s_0 \\ (s_1, s_2) = 1}} \Bigg\vert \sum_{f,k} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \\ \ell = h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2 \neq 0}} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{(c, s_0 s_1 s_2) = 1} \Phi\left(\frac{f}{F}, \frac{k}{K}, \frac{c}{C}\right) S(fk\overline{s_0 s_1 s_2}, a\ell; c) \Bigg\vert. \]
nodes.name: Extract gcd of s_1, s_2
nodes.statement_short: Pull out $s_0=(s_1,s_2)$ and reduce to $\mathcal K_1$.

nodes.statement: \mathcal{K}_0 \ll x^{o(1)} \sup_{S_0 \ll S} \mathcal{K}_1(S_0),
nodes.name: Equation (4.1) eq:K-split
nodes.label: eq:K-split

nodes.statement: We then put $n = |a\ell|$ and $r = s_0 s_1 s_2$ in dyadic ranges $n \sim \mathcal{N}$, $r \sim \mathcal{R}$, insert coefficients $\Psi(n/\mathcal{N})$ where $\Psi^{(j)} \ll_j 1$ and $\psi \equiv 1$ on $[1, 2]$, and use the divisor bound to write \begin{equation} \mathcal{K}_1 \ll x^{o(1)} \sup_{\substack{\mathcal{N} \ll_a HS/S_0 \\ \mathcal{R} \asymp S^2 / S_0}} \mathcal{K}_2(\mathcal{N}, \mathcal{R}), \end{equation} for \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathcal{K}_2 := \sum_{r \sim \mathcal{R}} \max_{\substack{s_0 \sim S_0 \\ s_1, s_2 \sim S/s_0 \\ (s_1, s_2) = 1 \\ s_0 s_1 s_2 = r}} \Bigg\vert \sum_{f,k} \sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \\ a(h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2) = \pm n}} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{(c, r) = 1} \Psi\left(\frac{n}{\mathcal{N}}\right) \Phi\left(\frac{f}{F}, \frac{k}{K}, \frac{c}{C} \right) S(fk\overline{r}, \pm n; c) \Bigg\vert, \end{aligned} \end{equation} where the supremum in \cref{eq:K1-split} includes the choice of the $\pm$ sign.
nodes.name: Dyadic decomposition
nodes.statement_short: Put $n$ and $r=s_0s_1s_2$ in dyadic ranges, reducing to $\mathcal K_2$.

nodes.statement: \mathcal{K}_1 \ll x^{o(1)} \sup_{\substack{\mathcal{N} \ll_a HS/S_0 \\ \mathcal{R} \asymp S^2 / S_0}} \mathcal{K}_2(\mathcal{N}, \mathcal{R}),
nodes.name: Equation (4.2) eq:K1-split
nodes.label: eq:K1-split

nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathcal{K}_2 := \sum_{r \sim \mathcal{R}} \max_{\substack{s_0 \sim S_0 \\ s_1, s_2 \sim S/s_0 \\ (s_1, s_2) = 1 \\ s_0 s_1 s_2 = r}} \Bigg\vert \sum_{f,k} \sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \\ a(h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2) = \pm n}} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{(c, r) = 1} \Psi\left(\frac{n}{\mathcal{N}}\right) \Phi\left(\frac{f}{F}, \frac{k}{K}, \frac{c}{C} \right) S(fk\overline{r}, \pm n; c) \Bigg\vert, \end{aligned}
nodes.name: Equation (4.3) eq:K2
nodes.label: eq:K2

nodes.statement: If the maximum above is attained at some $s_1(r), s_2(r)$, we let \[ a_{n,r} := \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \in \mathbb{Z} \\ a(h_1 s_1(r) - h_2 s_2(r)) = \pm n}} \phi(h_1, h_2) = \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \in \mathbb{Z} \\ \pm a(h_1 s_1(r) - h_2 s_2(r)) = n}} \Phi_1\left(\frac{h_1}{H}\right) \Phi_2\left(\frac{h_2}{H}\right) e(h_1\alpha_1 + h_2\alpha_2). \] If the maximum is empty, we let $a_{n, r} := 0$. Then we can rewrite \cref{eq:K2} as \[ \mathcal{K}_2 = \sum_{r \sim \mathcal{R}} \Bigg\vert \sum_{f,k} \sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} a_{n,r} \sum_{(c, r) = 1} \Psi\left(\frac{n}{\mathcal{N}}\right) \Phi\left(\frac{f}{F}, \frac{k}{K}, \frac{c}{C} \right) S(fk\overline{r}, \pm n; c) \Bigg\vert. \]
nodes.name: Define a_{n,r}
nodes.statement_short: Define the coefficients $a_{n,r}$ and rewrite $\mathcal K_2$.

nodes.statement: By \cref{prop:large-sieve-additive}, the tuple $(r, \mathcal{N}, x, (a_{n,r})_{n \sim \mathcal{N}}, A_r, Y)$ satisfies \cref{ass:large-sieve}, where \[ Y := \frac{\mathcal{N} H}{|a|(H+S/S_0)(S/S_0) \min_i T_H(\alpha_i)}, \qquad A_r := \left(\sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} |a_{n,r}|^2\right)^{1/2} + \sqrt{\mathcal{N}} \sqrt{\frac{H S_0}{S} + \frac{H^2 S_0^2}{S^2}}. \] Since $\min_i T_H(\alpha_i) \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon$, we further have \[ Y \gg_{\varepsilon,a} x^{-\varepsilon}\frac{\mathcal{N} H S_0}{(H+S)S}. \]
nodes.name: Additive large sieve
nodes.statement_short: Prop. 3.4 gives the large sieve assumption with saving $Y$.

nodes.statement: We can now apply \cref{prop:kloosterman-complete}; specifically, by \cref{eq:kloosterman-rsm12nc}, we obtain \[ \mathcal{K}_2 \ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{O(\varepsilon)} \left(1 + \frac{C\sqrt{F}}{\mathcal{R}\sqrt{\frac{\mathcal{N} H S_0}{(H+S)S}}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \|A_r\|_2 \sqrt{\mathcal{R} F K} \left(\frac{C^2}{\mathcal{R}}(FK + \mathcal{R})(\mathcal{N} + \mathcal{R}) + FK\mathcal{N}\right)^{1/2}. \]
nodes.name: Kloosterman bound
nodes.statement_short: Apply Prop. 3.8 to bound $\mathcal K_2$.

nodes.statement: We claim that \begin{equation} \|A_r\|_2^2 \ll x^{o(1)} \mathcal{N}(HS + H^2 S_0). \end{equation} Indeed, this follows from the definition of $A_r$ and the two bounds \[ \sum_{r \sim \mathcal{R}} \mathcal{N} \left(\frac{HS_0}{S} + \frac{H^2 S_0^2}{S^2}\right) \asymp \frac{S^2}{S_0} \mathcal{N} \left(\frac{HS_0}{S} + \frac{H^2 S_0^2}{S^2}\right) \asymp \mathcal{N} (HS + H^2 S_0), \] \[ \begin{aligned} \sum_{r \sim \mathcal{R}} \sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} |a_{n,r}|^2 &\ll \sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} \sum_{s_0 \sim S_0} \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S/s_0 \\ (s_1, s_2) = 1}} \left( \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \asymp H \\ h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2 = \pm n/a}} 1 \right)^2 \\ &\ll \sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} \sum_{s_0 \sim S_0} \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S/s_0 \\ (s_1, s_2) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \asymp H \\ h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2 = \pm n/a}}\, \sum_{\substack{h_1', h_2' \asymp H \\ s_1(h_1 - h_1') = s_2(h_2 - h_2')}} 1 \\ &\ll \sum_{n \sim \mathcal{N}} \sum_{s_0 \sim S_0} \sum_{\substack{s_1 \sim S/s_0 \\ h_1 \asymp H}} \sum_{\substack{s_2 \sim S/s_0 \\ h_2 \asymp H \\ h_2 s_2 = h_1 s_1 \mp n/a}} \sum_{\substack{h_1' \asymp H \\ h_1' \equiv h_1 \pmod{s_2}}}\, \sum_{\substack{h_2' \asymp H \\ s_1(h_1 - h_1') = s_2(h_2 - h_2')}} 1 \\ &\ll x^{o(1)} \mathcal{N} S_0 \frac{S}{S_0} H \left(1 + \frac{H S_0}{S}\right) \quad = x^{o(1)} \mathcal{N} (HS + H^2 S_0). \end{aligned} \]
nodes.name: l2 bound for A_r
nodes.statement_short: Show $\|A_r\|_2^2\ll x^{o(1)}\mathcal N(HS+H^2S_0)$ by counting solutions.

nodes.statement: \|A_r\|_2^2 \ll x^{o(1)} \mathcal{N}(HS + H^2 S_0).
nodes.name: Equation (4.4) eq:primes-l2-bound
nodes.label: eq:primes-l2-bound

nodes.statement: Using \cref{eq:primes-l2-bound}, we can further bound \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{K}_2 &\ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{O(\varepsilon)} \\ &\times \left(1 + \frac{C\sqrt{F}}{\mathcal{R}\sqrt{\frac{\mathcal{N} H S_0}{(H+S)S}}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \sqrt{\mathcal{N} (HS + H^2 S_0) \mathcal{R} F K} \left(\frac{C^2}{\mathcal{R}}(FK + \mathcal{R})(\mathcal{N} + \mathcal{R}) + FK\mathcal{N}\right)^{1/2}, \end{aligned} \] where the right-hand side is increasing in $\mathcal{N} \ll_a HS/S_0$. Substituting this value of $\mathcal{N}$ and $\mathcal{R} \asymp S^2/S_0$, it follows from \cref{eq:K1-split} that \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal{K}_1 &\ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{O(\varepsilon)} \left(1 + \frac{C\sqrt{F}}{\frac{S^2}{S_0}\sqrt{\frac{H^2}{H+S}}}\right)^{\theta_{\max}} \\ &\times \sqrt{\frac{HS}{S_0} (HS + H^2 S_0) \frac{S^2}{S_0} F K} \left(\frac{C^2 S_0}{S^2}\left(FK + \frac{S^2}{S_0}\right)\left(\frac{HS}{S_0} + \frac{S^2}{S_0}\right) + \frac{FKHS}{S_0}\right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \]

nodes.statement: Since $\theta_{\max} < 1/2$, the right-hand side is seen to be decreasing in $S_0 \gg 1$; substituting $S_0$ with $1$ and plugging this into \cref{eq:K-split}, we obtain the desired bound for $\mathcal{K}_0$.

nodes.statement: Let $a \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, $d \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ with $(a, d) = 1$, $\varepsilon, C > 0$, and $M, N, x, Q, R, S \gg 1$ satisfy $MN \asymp x$ and, with $\theta := 7/32$, \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} N^2 R^2 S &\le x^{1-8\varepsilon}, \\ N^{\frac{2+\theta}{2-2\theta}} R S^{\frac{4-5\theta}{2-2\theta}} &\le x^{1-16\varepsilon}, \\ N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} Q^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} R^{2} S^{5} &\le x^{2-32\varepsilon}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Let $Q' \in [Q, 2Q]$, $1 \ll H \le x^{o(1)} Q R^2 S^2/M$, $B_i \gg 1$, and let $\mathscr{N} \subset \mathbb{Z}_+^2$ be such that if $(u; v), (u'; v') \in \mathscr{N}$, then $(u, v') = (u', v) = 1$. Finally, let $(\gamma_r)$, $(\lambda_s)$, $(\alpha_n)$ be $1$-bounded sequences, $\omega \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ with $T_H(\omega) \ll x^{o(1)}$, and $\Phi(t)$ be a smooth function supported in $t \asymp 1$, with $\Phi^{(j)} \ll_j 1$ for $j \ge 0$. Then \[ \begin{aligned} \sum_{\substack{Q \le q \le Q' \\ (q, a) = 1}} \sum_{r_1, r_2 \sim R} \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S \\ (r_1s_1, ar_2s_2) = 1 \\ (r_2 s_2, a q d r_1 s_1) = 1 \\ r_i s_i \le B_i}} \frac{\gamma_{r_1} \lambda_{s_1} \overline{\gamma_{r_2}\lambda_{s_2}}}{r_1 r_2 s_1 s_2 q} \sum_{\substack{n_1, n_2 \sim N \\ n_1 \equiv n_2 \pmod{qd} \\ (n_1, n_2 q d r_1 s_1) = 1 \\ (n_2, n_1 q d r_2 s_2) = 1 \\ (n_1 r_2 s_2; n_2) \in \mathscr{N} \\ |n_1 - n_2| \ge N/(\log x)^C}} \alpha_{n_1} \overline{\alpha_{n_2}}& \\ \times \sum_{h \in \mathbb{Z}} e(h\omega)\, \Phi\left(\frac{h}{H}\right) e\left(\frac{ah(n_1 - n_2) \overline{n_2 r_1 s_1 dq}}{n_1 r_2 s_2}\right)& \ll_{a,\varepsilon,C} \frac{N^2}{Qx^\varepsilon}. \end{aligned} \]

We closely follow the proof of \cite[Lemma 7.1]{maynard2025primes2}, taking $Q \ll N$ without loss of generality (otherwise the sum over $n_1, n_2$ vanishes). After the substitution $f d q = n_1 - n_2$, a separation of variables and an application of Cauchy--Schwarz in $f, n_1, n_2, r_1, r_2, s_2$, we reach the sum \[ \mathscr{W}_4 := \sum_{\substack{b, c, f \ (b, c) = 1}} \Psi_0\left( rac{b}{B}ight) \Psi_0\left( rac{c}{C_0}ight) \Psi_0\left( rac{f}{F_0}ight) \left\vert \sum_{s \sim S} \lambda_s' \sum_{h \in \mathbb{Z}} e(h\omega)\, \Phi\left( rac{h_1}{H}ight) e\left( rac{ahf\overline{bs}}{c}ight) ight\vert^2, \] similar to \cite[p.\,23, third display]{maynard2025primes2}. Here we also inserted a smooth majorant in the $f$ variable, where $\Psi_0$ is a compactly-supported nonnegative function satisfying $\Psi_0^{(j)} \ll_j 1$. As in \cite[p.\,23, second display]{maynard2025primes2}, the ranges $B, C_0, F_0$ satisfy  egin{equation} B \ll NR, \qquad C_0 \ll NRS, \qquad F_0 \ll  rac{N}{Q}, \end{equation} and as in \cite[(7.4)]{maynard2025primes2}, we need to show that $\mathscr{W}_4 \ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{-6\varepsilon} N^2 R^2 S^3$. Normally at this stage, we would expand the square in $\mathscr{W}_4$, leading to a sum like in \cref{eq:incomplete-kloosterman-overview}, and then complete Kloosterman sums. But as outlined in \cref{subsec:improvements}, to achieve good savings in the complementary divisor ($f \sim F$) aspect, we will need to `move' $f$ to the other entry of the resulting Kloosterman sums. Towards this goal, we split the sum according to the value of $d = (f, c)$:  egin{equation} \mathscr{W}_4 \le \sum_{1 \le d \ll x} \mathscr{W}_5(d), \end{equation} where, after relaxing the constraint $(b, c) = 1$ to $(b, c/d) = 1$, substituting $(f, c) \gets (fd, cd)$, and letting  egin{equation} C :=  rac{C_0}{d}, \qquad\qquad F :=  rac{F_0}{d}, \end{equation} we have \[ \mathscr{W}_5 := \sum_{\substack{b, c, f \ (bf, c) = 1}} \Psi_0\left( rac{b}{B}ight) \Psi_0\left( rac{c}{C}ight) \Psi_0\left( rac{f}{F}ight) \left\vert \sum_{\substack{s \sim S \ (s, c) = 1}} \lambda_s' \sum_{h \in \mathbb{Z}} e(h\omega)\, \Phi\left( rac{h_1}{H}ight) e\left( rac{ahf\overline{bs}}{c}ight) ight\vert^2. \] Due to \cref{eq:W4-split} and $\sum_{1 \le d \ll x}  rac{1}{d} \ll \log x$, it is enough to show that  egin{equation} \mathscr{W}_5 \ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{-7\varepsilon}  rac{N^2 R^2 S^3}{d}. \end{equation} Now let \[ \mathscr{W}(x; c) := \sum_{\substack{s \sim S \ (s, c) = 1}} \lambda_s' \sum_{h \in \mathbb{Z}} e(h\omega)\, \Phi\left( rac{h_1}{H}ight) e\left( rac{ah\overline{xs}}{c}ight), \] for $x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^	imes$, so we can write \[  egin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_5 &= \sum_{c} \Psi_0\left( rac{c}{C}ight) \sum_{(f, c) = 1} \Psi_0\left( rac{f}{F}ight) \sum_{(b, c) = 1} \Psi_0\left( rac{b}{B}ight) |\mathscr{W}(b\overline{f}; c)|^2 \ &= \sum_c \Psi_0\left( rac{c}{C}ight) \sum_{(f, c) = 1} \Psi_0\left( rac{f}{F}ight) \sum_{x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^	imes} |\mathscr{W}(x; c)|^2 \sum_{b \equiv xf \pmod{c}} \Psi_0\left( rac{b}{B}ight) \ &\le \sum_c \Psi_0\left( rac{c}{C}ight) \sum_{f} \Psi_0\left( rac{f}{F}ight) \sum_{x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^	imes} |\mathscr{W}(x; c)|^2 \sum_{b \equiv xf \pmod{c}} \Psi_0\left( rac{b}{B}ight), \end{aligned} \] where we dropped the restriction $(f, c) = 1$ in the last line. Expanding the square and swapping sums, we get \[  egin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_5 \le \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S \ (s_1 s_2, a) = 1}} \lambda'_{s_1} \overline{\lambda'_{s_2}} \sum_{h_1, h_2} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{f} \Psi_0\left( rac{f}{F}ight) \sum_{(c, s_1s_2) = 1} \Psi_0\left( rac{c}{C}ight) \ 	imes \sum_{x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^	imes} e\left( rac{a\ell \overline{s_1s_2 x}}{c}ight) \sum_{b \equiv xf \pmod{c}} \Psi_0\left( rac{b}{B}ight), \end{aligned} \] where  egin{equation} \ell := h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2, \qquad \phi(h_1, h_2) := e((h_1 - h_2)\omega)\, \Phi\left( rac{h_1}{H}ight) \overline{\Phi\left( rac{h_2}{H}ight)}. \end{equation} Splitting the sum above into the terms with $\ell = 0$ and $\ell 
eq 0$, we have  egin{equation} \mathscr{W}_5 \le \mathscr{W}_{\ell=0} + \mathscr{W}_{\ell 
eq 0}. \end{equation} In light of \cref{eq:bcf-bounds,eq:cf-substitution}, the diagonal terms contribute at most  egin{equation}  egin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_{\ell = 0} &\ll \sum_{s_1, s_2 \sim S} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \asymp H \ h_1 s_1 = h_2 s_2}} \sum_{f \asymp F} \sum_{c \asymp C} \sum_{b \asymp B} \sum_{x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^	imes} \mathbbm{1}_{b \equiv xf \pmod{c}} \ &\ll \sum_{s_1, s_2 \sim S} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \asymp H \ h_1 s_1 = h_2 s_2}} \sum_{f \asymp F} \sum_{c \asymp C} \sum_{b \asymp B} (b, c, f) \ &\ll x^{o(1)} S H F C B \ &\ll x^{o(1)} S  rac{Q R^2 S^2}{x/N}  rac{N}{dQ}  rac{NRS}{d} NR \ll  rac{N^4 R^4 S^4}{d^2 x^{1-\varepsilon}}, \end{aligned} \end{equation} and this is acceptable in \cref{eq:W5-bound-to-show} provided that \[ N^2 R^2 S \ll_\varepsilon x^{1-8\varepsilon}, \] which we assumed in \cref{eq:ranges-qrs}. For the off-diagonal terms, which roughly correspond to \cref{eq:incomplete-kloosterman-overview}, we complete the inner sum over $b$ via \cref{lem:truncated-poisson} to obtain  egin{equation}  egin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_{\ell

eq 0}} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{f} \Psi_0\left( rac{f}{F}ight) \sum_{(c, s_1s_2) = 1} \Psi_0\left( rac{c}{C}ight) \sum_{x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^	imes} e\left( rac{a\ell \overline{s_1s_2 x}}{c}ight) \ 	imes  rac{B}{C} \Psi_0\left( rac{uc}{C}ight) \sum_k \Psi\left( rac{|k|}{K}ight) e\left(-k rac{uB}{C}ight) e\left( rac{xfk}{c}ight). \end{aligned} \] We first bound $\mathscr{W}_6$ using the Ramanujan sum bound (see \cref{lem:weil}), \cref{eq:bcf-bounds,eq:cf-substitution}:  egin{equation}  egin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_6 &= \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S \ (s_1 s_2, a) = 1}} \lambda'_{s_1} \overline{\lambda'_{s_2}} \sum_{h_1, h_2} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{f} \Psi_0\left( rac{f}{F}ight) \sum_{(c, s_1s_2) = 1} \Psi_0\left( rac{c}{C}ight) S(0, a\ell; c)  rac{B}{c} \widehat{\Psi_0}(0) \ &\ll \sum_{s_1, s_2 \sim S} \sum_{h_1, h_2 \asymp H} \sum_{f \asymp F} \sum_{c \asymp C} (a\ell, c)  rac{B}{c} \ &\ll_a x^{o(1)} S^2 H^2 F B \ &\ll x^{o(1)} S^2 \left( rac{QR^2 S^2}{x/N}ight)^2  rac{N}{dQ} NR \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon  rac{Q R^5 S^6 N^4}{dx^2}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} This is acceptable in \cref{eq:W5-bound-to-show} (i.e., $\ll_\varepsilon x^{-7\varepsilon} N^2 R^2 S^3/d$) provided that \[ N^2 Q R^3 S^3 \ll x^{2-8\varepsilon}, \] which follows from $Q \ll N$ and the first and third assumptions in \cref{eq:ranges-qrs}: \[  egin{aligned} N^2 Q R^3 S^3 &\ll N^3 R^3 S^3 \ &\le \left(N^2 R^2 Sight)^{4/3} \cdot \left(N R^2 S^5ight)^{1/3} \le \left(x^{1-8\varepsilon}ight)^{4/3} \left(x^{2-32\varepsilon}ight)^{1/3} < x^{2-8\varepsilon}. \end{aligned} \] We are left to consider $\mathscr{W}_7$, which roughly corresponds to the sum in \cref{eq:sum-kloosterman-overview}, and can be rewritten as \[  egin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_7 =  rac{B}{C} \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S \ (s_1 s_2, a) = 1}} \lambda'_{s_1} \overline{\lambda'_{s_2}} \sum_{f,k} \Psi_0\left( rac{f}{F}ight) \Psi\left( rac{|k|}{K}ight) e\left(-k rac{uB}{C}ight) \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \ \ell = h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2 
eq 0}} \phi(h_1, h_2) \ 	imes \sum_{(c, s_1s_2) = 1} \Psi_0\left( rac{c}{C}ight) \Psi_0\left( rac{uc}{C}ight) S(fk\overline{s_1 s_2}, a\ell; c). \end{aligned} \] We can now apply \cref{lem:consequence-Kloosterman} with the smooth weight \[ \Phi\left(x_1, x_2, zight) := \Psi_0\left(x_1ight) \Psi\left(x_2ight) e\left(\mp x_2 rac{uKB}{C}ight) \Psi_0\left(zight) \Psi_0\left(uzight), \] once for each choice of the $\pm$ sign (corresponding to the sign of $k$; note that $S(-fk\overline{s_1 s_2}, a\ell; c) = S(fk\overline{s_1 s_2}, -a\ell; c)$, so one can transfer the sign change to $a$ without loss of generality).
