&\ll_{\varepsilon,a}  rac{x^\varepsilon}{d} \left( rac{N^3 R^3 S^5}{x} \left(1 + \left( rac{x\sqrt{N}}{R S^{5/2}} ight)^{	heta}ight) +  rac{N^{5/2} Q^{1/2} R^3 S^{11/2}}{x} \left(1 + \left( rac{x\sqrt{N}}{R S^{5/2} Q^{3/2}} ight)^{	heta}ight)ight), \end{aligned} \] where we omitted a factor of $Q^{-3	heta/2}$ in the second term of the expansion. For this to be acceptable in \cref{eq:W5-bound-to-show} (i.e., $\ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{-7\varepsilon} N^2 R^2 S^3 / d$), we need the following restrictions: \[  egin{gathered} N R S^2 \ll x^{1-8\varepsilon}, \qquad\qquad N^{2+	heta} R^{2-2	heta} S^{4-5	heta} \ll x^{2-2	heta-16\varepsilon}, \ N Q R^2 S^5 \ll x^{2-16\varepsilon}, \qquad\qquad N^{1+	heta} Q^{1-3	heta} R^{2-2	heta} S^{5-5	heta} \ll x^{2-2	heta-16\varepsilon}. \end{gathered} \] All of these restrictions follow from \cref{eq:ranges-qrs}, $Q \ll N$, and $	heta \le 1/2$, as shown below: \[  egin{aligned} NRS^2 &\le \left(N^2 R^2 S \cdot N R^2 S^5 ight)^{1/3} \le \left(x^{1-8\varepsilon} \cdot x^{2-32\varepsilon}ight)^{1/3} < x^{1-8\varepsilon}, \ N Q R^2 S^5 &\ll \left( rac{N}{Q}ight)^{ rac{2	heta}{1-	heta}} N Q R^2 S^5 = N^{ rac{1+	heta}{1-	heta}} Q^{ rac{1-3	heta}{1-	heta}} R^2 S^5 < x^{2-16\varepsilon}, \ N^{2+	heta} R^{2-2	heta} S^{4-5	heta} &= \left(N^{ rac{2+	heta}{2-2	heta}} R S^{ rac{4-5	heta}{2-2	heta}}ight)^{2-2	heta} \le (x^{1-16\varepsilon})^{2-2	heta} \le x^{2-2	heta-16\varepsilon}, \ N^{1+	heta} Q^{1-3	heta} R^{2-2	heta} S^{5-5	heta} &= \left(N^{ rac{1+	heta}{1-	heta}} Q^{ rac{1-3	heta}{1-	heta}} R^{2} S^5ight)^{1-	heta} \le (x^{2-32\varepsilon})^{1-	heta} \le x^{2-2	heta-16\varepsilon}. \end{aligned} \] In light of \cref{eq:W5-split,eq:W-diagonal-bound,eq:W-off-diagonal-split,eq:W6-bound}, this establishes \cref{eq:W5-bound-to-show} and completes our proof.
nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Follow Maynard's Lemma 7.1: Cauchy–Schwarz, split by $(f,c)$ to move $f$ into the Kloosterman sum, Poisson-complete in $b$. The off-diagonal terms are bounded via Lemma 4.1.

nodes.statement: We closely follow the proof of \cite[Lemma 7.1]{maynard2025primes2}, taking $Q \ll N$ without loss of generality (otherwise the sum over $n_1, n_2$ vanishes).
nodes.name: Follow Maynard Lemma 7.1
nodes.statement_short: WLOG $Q\ll N$; follow Maynard's argument.

nodes.statement: After the substitution $f d q = n_1 - n_2$, a separation of variables and an application of Cauchy--Schwarz in $f, n_1, n_2, r_1, r_2, s_2$, we reach the sum \[ \mathscr{W}_4 := \sum_{\substack{b, c, f \\ (b, c) = 1}} \Psi_0\left(\frac{b}{B}\right) \Psi_0\left(\frac{c}{C_0}\right) \Psi_0\left(\frac{f}{F_0}\right) \left\vert \sum_{s \sim S} \lambda_s' \sum_{h \in \mathbb{Z}} e(h\omega)\, \Phi\left(\frac{h_1}{H}\right) e\left(\frac{ahf\overline{bs}}{c}\right) \right\vert^2, \] similar to \cite[p.\,23, third display]{maynard2025primes2}.
nodes.name: Cauchy–Schwarz to W_4
nodes.statement_short: Substitute and apply Cauchy–Schwarz to reach $\mathscr W_4$.

nodes.statement: Here we also inserted a smooth majorant in the $f$ variable, where $\Psi_0$ is a compactly-supported nonnegative function satisfying $\Psi_0^{(j)} \ll_j 1$. As in \cite[p.\,23, second display]{maynard2025primes2}, the ranges $B, C_0, F_0$ satisfy \begin{equation} B \ll NR, \qquad C_0 \ll NRS, \qquad F_0 \ll \frac{N}{Q}, \end{equation} and as in \cite[(7.4)]{maynard2025primes2}, we need to show that $\mathscr{W}_4 \ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{-6\varepsilon} N^2 R^2 S^3$.
nodes.name: Target bound for W_4
nodes.statement_short: Record ranges (4.6) and the target bound for $\mathscr W_4$.

nodes.statement: B \ll NR, \qquad C_0 \ll NRS, \qquad F_0 \ll \frac{N}{Q},
nodes.name: Equation (4.6) eq:bcf-bounds
nodes.label: eq:bcf-bounds

nodes.statement: Normally at this stage, we would expand the square in $\mathscr{W}_4$, leading to a sum like in \cref{eq:incomplete-kloosterman-overview}, and then complete Kloosterman sums. But as outlined in \cref{subsec:improvements}, to achieve good savings in the complementary divisor ($f \sim F$) aspect, we will need to `move' $f$ to the other entry of the resulting Kloosterman sums. Towards this goal, we split the sum according to the value of $d = (f, c)$: \begin{equation} \mathscr{W}_4 \le \sum_{1 \le d \ll x} \mathscr{W}_5(d), \end{equation} where, after relaxing the constraint $(b, c) = 1$ to $(b, c/d) = 1$, substituting $(f, c) \gets (fd, cd)$, and letting \begin{equation} C := \frac{C_0}{d}, \qquad\qquad F := \frac{F_0}{d}, \end{equation} we have \[ \mathscr{W}_5 := \sum_{\substack{b, c, f \\ (bf, c) = 1}} \Psi_0\left(\frac{b}{B}\right) \Psi_0\left(\frac{c}{C}\right) \Psi_0\left(\frac{f}{F}\right) \left\vert \sum_{\substack{s \sim S \\ (s, c) = 1}} \lambda_s' \sum_{h \in \mathbb{Z}} e(h\omega)\, \Phi\left(\frac{h_1}{H}\right) e\left(\frac{ahf\overline{bs}}{c}\right) \right\vert^2. \]
nodes.name: Split by d = (f, c)
nodes.statement_short: Split by $d=(f,c)$ to move $f$ to the other entry of the Kloosterman sums.

nodes.statement: \mathscr{W}_4 \le \sum_{1 \le d \ll x} \mathscr{W}_5(d),
nodes.name: Equation (4.7) eq:W4-split
nodes.label: eq:W4-split

nodes.statement: C := \frac{C_0}{d}, \qquad\qquad F := \frac{F_0}{d},
nodes.name: Equation (4.8) eq:cf-substitution
nodes.label: eq:cf-substitution

nodes.statement: Due to \cref{eq:W4-split} and $\sum_{1 \le d \ll x} \frac{1}{d} \ll \log x$, it is enough to show that \begin{equation} \mathscr{W}_5 \ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{-7\varepsilon} \frac{N^2 R^2 S^3}{d}. \end{equation}
nodes.name: Reduce to W_5 bound
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to prove (4.9) for each $d$.

nodes.statement: \mathscr{W}_5 \ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{-7\varepsilon} \frac{N^2 R^2 S^3}{d}.
nodes.name: Equation (4.9) eq:W5-bound-to-show
nodes.label: eq:W5-bound-to-show

nodes.statement: Now let \[ \mathscr{W}(x; c) := \sum_{\substack{s \sim S \\ (s, c) = 1}} \lambda_s' \sum_{h \in \mathbb{Z}} e(h\omega)\, \Phi\left(\frac{h_1}{H}\right) e\left(\frac{ah\overline{xs}}{c}\right), \] for $x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^\times$, so we can write \[ \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_5 &= \sum_{c} \Psi_0\left(\frac{c}{C}\right) \sum_{(f, c) = 1} \Psi_0\left(\frac{f}{F}\right) \sum_{(b, c) = 1} \Psi_0\left(\frac{b}{B}\right) |\mathscr{W}(b\overline{f}; c)|^2 \\ &= \sum_c \Psi_0\left(\frac{c}{C}\right) \sum_{(f, c) = 1} \Psi_0\left(\frac{f}{F}\right) \sum_{x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^\times} |\mathscr{W}(x; c)|^2 \sum_{b \equiv xf \pmod{c}} \Psi_0\left(\frac{b}{B}\right) \\ &\le \sum_c \Psi_0\left(\frac{c}{C}\right) \sum_{f} \Psi_0\left(\frac{f}{F}\right) \sum_{x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^\times} |\mathscr{W}(x; c)|^2 \sum_{b \equiv xf \pmod{c}} \Psi_0\left(\frac{b}{B}\right), \end{aligned} \] where we dropped the restriction $(f, c) = 1$ in the last line.
nodes.name: Introduce W(x; c)
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $\mathscr W_5$ via $\mathscr W(x;c)$ and drop $(f,c)=1$.

nodes.statement: Expanding the square and swapping sums, we get \[ \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_5 \le \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S \\ (s_1 s_2, a) = 1}} \lambda'_{s_1} \overline{\lambda'_{s_2}} \sum_{h_1, h_2} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{f} \Psi_0\left(\frac{f}{F}\right) \sum_{(c, s_1s_2) = 1} \Psi_0\left(\frac{c}{C}\right) \\ \times \sum_{x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^\times} e\left(\frac{a\ell \overline{s_1s_2 x}}{c}\right) \sum_{b \equiv xf \pmod{c}} \Psi_0\left(\frac{b}{B}\right), \end{aligned} \] where \begin{equation} \ell := h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2, \qquad \phi(h_1, h_2) := e((h_1 - h_2)\omega)\, \Phi\left(\frac{h_1}{H}\right) \overline{\Phi\left(\frac{h_2}{H}\right)}. \end{equation} Splitting the sum above into the terms with $\ell = 0$ and $\ell \neq 0$, we have \begin{equation} \mathscr{W}_5 \le \mathscr{W}_{\ell=0} + \mathscr{W}_{\ell \neq 0}. \end{equation}
nodes.name: Expand square; split l = 0
nodes.statement_short: Expand, swap sums and split into $\ell=0$ and $\ell\neq0$.

nodes.statement: \ell := h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2, \qquad \phi(h_1, h_2) := e((h_1 - h_2)\omega)\, \Phi\left(\frac{h_1}{H}\right) \overline{\Phi\left(\frac{h_2}{H}\right)}.
nodes.name: Equation (4.10) eq:smooth-in-h
nodes.label: eq:smooth-in-h

nodes.statement: \mathscr{W}_5 \le \mathscr{W}_{\ell=0} + \mathscr{W}_{\ell \neq 0}.
nodes.name: Equation (4.11) eq:W5-split
nodes.label: eq:W5-split

nodes.statement: In light of \cref{eq:bcf-bounds,eq:cf-substitution}, the diagonal terms contribute at most \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_{\ell = 0} &\ll \sum_{s_1, s_2 \sim S} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \asymp H \\ h_1 s_1 = h_2 s_2}} \sum_{f \asymp F} \sum_{c \asymp C} \sum_{b \asymp B} \sum_{x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^\times} \mathbbm{1}_{b \equiv xf \pmod{c}} \\ &\ll \sum_{s_1, s_2 \sim S} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \asymp H \\ h_1 s_1 = h_2 s_2}} \sum_{f \asymp F} \sum_{c \asymp C} \sum_{b \asymp B} (b, c, f) \\ &\ll x^{o(1)} S H F C B \\ &\ll x^{o(1)} S \frac{Q R^2 S^2}{x/N} \frac{N}{dQ} \frac{NRS}{d} NR \ll \frac{N^4 R^4 S^4}{d^2 x^{1-\varepsilon}}, \end{aligned} \end{equation} and this is acceptable in \cref{eq:W5-bound-to-show} provided that \[ N^2 R^2 S \ll_\varepsilon x^{1-8\varepsilon}, \] which we assumed in \cref{eq:ranges-qrs}.
nodes.name: Diagonal terms
nodes.statement_short: Bound the diagonal terms, acceptable under the first range condition.

nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_{\ell = 0} &\ll \sum_{s_1, s_2 \sim S} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \asymp H \\ h_1 s_1 = h_2 s_2}} \sum_{f \asymp F} \sum_{c \asymp C} \sum_{b \asymp B} \sum_{x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^\times} \mathbbm{1}_{b \equiv xf \pmod{c}} \\ &\ll \sum_{s_1, s_2 \sim S} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \asymp H \\ h_1 s_1 = h_2 s_2}} \sum_{f \asymp F} \sum_{c \asymp C} \sum_{b \asymp B} (b, c, f) \\ &\ll x^{o(1)} S H F C B \\ &\ll x^{o(1)} S \frac{Q R^2 S^2}{x/N} \frac{N}{dQ} \frac{NRS}{d} NR \ll \frac{N^4 R^4 S^4}{d^2 x^{1-\varepsilon}}, \end{aligned}
nodes.name: Equation (4.12) eq:W-diagonal-bound
nodes.label: eq:W-diagonal-bound

nodes.statement: For the off-diagonal terms, which roughly correspond to \cref{eq:incomplete-kloosterman-overview}, we complete the inner sum over $b$ via \cref{lem:truncated-poisson} to obtain \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_{\ell \neq 0} \ll |\mathscr{W}_6| + O(x^{-90}) + x^{o(1)} \sup_{\substack{K \ll x^{o(1)} B^{-1} C \\ \Psi^{(k)} \ll_k 1 \\ u \asymp 1}} |\mathscr{W}_7(K, u)|, \end{aligned} \end{equation} where $\Psi$ is a smooth function supported in $(\frac{1}{2}, 2)$, \[ \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_6 := \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S \\ (s_1 s_2, a) = 1}} \lambda'_{s_1} \overline{\lambda'_{s_2}} \sum_{h_1, h_2} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{f} \Psi_0\left(\frac{f}{F}\right) \sum_{(c, s_1s_2) = 1} \Psi_0\left(\frac{c}{C}\right) \sum_{x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^\times} e\left(\frac{a\ell \overline{s_1s_2 x}}{c}\right) \\ \times \frac{B}{c} \widehat{\Psi_0}(0) \end{aligned} \] is the contribution of the principal frequency, and \[ \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_7 := \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S \\ (s_1 s_2, a) = 1}} \lambda'_{s_1} \overline{\lambda'_{s_2}} \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \\ \ell = h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2 \neq 0}} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{f} \Psi_0\left(\frac{f}{F}\right) \sum_{(c, s_1s_2) = 1} \Psi_0\left(\frac{c}{C}\right) \sum_{x \in (\mathbb{Z}/c\mathbb{Z})^\times} e\left(\frac{a\ell \overline{s_1s_2 x}}{c}\right) \\ \times \frac{B}{C} \Psi_0\left(\frac{uc}{C}\right) \sum_k \Psi\left(\frac{|k|}{K}\right) e\left(-k\frac{uB}{C}\right) e\left(\frac{xfk}{c}\right). \end{aligned} \]
nodes.name: Poisson completion in b
nodes.statement_short: Complete the sum over $b$ by Lemma 3.1 into $\mathscr W_6$ and $\mathscr W_7$.

nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_{\ell \neq 0} \ll |\mathscr{W}_6| + O(x^{-90}) + x^{o(1)} \sup_{\substack{K \ll x^{o(1)} B^{-1} C \\ \Psi^{(k)} \ll_k 1 \\ u \asymp 1}} |\mathscr{W}_7(K, u)|, \end{aligned}
nodes.name: Equation (4.13) eq:W-off-diagonal-split
nodes.label: eq:W-off-diagonal-split

nodes.statement: We first bound $\mathscr{W}_6$ using the Ramanujan sum bound (see \cref{lem:weil}), \cref{eq:bcf-bounds,eq:cf-substitution}: \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_6 &= \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S \\ (s_1 s_2, a) = 1}} \lambda'_{s_1} \overline{\lambda'_{s_2}} \sum_{h_1, h_2} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{f} \Psi_0\left(\frac{f}{F}\right) \sum_{(c, s_1s_2) = 1} \Psi_0\left(\frac{c}{C}\right) S(0, a\ell; c) \frac{B}{c} \widehat{\Psi_0}(0) \\ &\ll \sum_{s_1, s_2 \sim S} \sum_{h_1, h_2 \asymp H} \sum_{f \asymp F} \sum_{c \asymp C} (a\ell, c) \frac{B}{c} \\ &\ll_a x^{o(1)} S^2 H^2 F B \\ &\ll x^{o(1)} S^2 \left(\frac{QR^2 S^2}{x/N}\right)^2 \frac{N}{dQ} NR \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon \frac{Q R^5 S^6 N^4}{dx^2}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} This is acceptable in \cref{eq:W5-bound-to-show} (i.e., $\ll_\varepsilon x^{-7\varepsilon} N^2 R^2 S^3/d$) provided that \[ N^2 Q R^3 S^3 \ll x^{2-8\varepsilon}, \] which follows from $Q \ll N$ and the first and third assumptions in \cref{eq:ranges-qrs}: \[ \begin{aligned} N^2 Q R^3 S^3 &\ll N^3 R^3 S^3 \\ &\le \left(N^2 R^2 S\right)^{4/3} \cdot \left(N R^2 S^5\right)^{1/3} \le \left(x^{1-8\varepsilon}\right)^{4/3} \left(x^{2-32\varepsilon}\right)^{1/3} < x^{2-8\varepsilon}. \end{aligned} \]
nodes.name: Bound W_6
nodes.statement_short: Bound the principal frequency via the Ramanujan sum bound.

nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_6 &= \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S \\ (s_1 s_2, a) = 1}} \lambda'_{s_1} \overline{\lambda'_{s_2}} \sum_{h_1, h_2} \phi(h_1, h_2) \sum_{f} \Psi_0\left(\frac{f}{F}\right) \sum_{(c, s_1s_2) = 1} \Psi_0\left(\frac{c}{C}\right) S(0, a\ell; c) \frac{B}{c} \widehat{\Psi_0}(0) \\ &\ll \sum_{s_1, s_2 \sim S} \sum_{h_1, h_2 \asymp H} \sum_{f \asymp F} \sum_{c \asymp C} (a\ell, c) \frac{B}{c} \\ &\ll_a x^{o(1)} S^2 H^2 F B \\ &\ll x^{o(1)} S^2 \left(\frac{QR^2 S^2}{x/N}\right)^2 \frac{N}{dQ} NR \ll_\varepsilon x^\varepsilon \frac{Q R^5 S^6 N^4}{dx^2}. \end{aligned}
nodes.name: Equation (4.14) eq:W6-bound
nodes.label: eq:W6-bound

nodes.statement: We are left to consider $\mathscr{W}_7$, which roughly corresponds to the sum in \cref{eq:sum-kloosterman-overview}, and can be rewritten as \[ \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_7 = \frac{B}{C} \sum_{\substack{s_1, s_2 \sim S \\ (s_1 s_2, a) = 1}} \lambda'_{s_1} \overline{\lambda'_{s_2}} \sum_{f,k} \Psi_0\left(\frac{f}{F}\right) \Psi\left(\frac{|k|}{K}\right) e\left(-k\frac{uB}{C}\right) \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \\ \ell = h_1 s_1 - h_2 s_2 \neq 0}} \phi(h_1, h_2) \\ \times \sum_{(c, s_1s_2) = 1} \Psi_0\left(\frac{c}{C}\right) \Psi_0\left(\frac{uc}{C}\right) S(fk\overline{s_1 s_2}, a\ell; c). \end{aligned} \]
nodes.name: Rewrite W_7
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $\mathscr W_7$ as a sum of Kloosterman sums.

nodes.statement: We can now apply \cref{lem:consequence-Kloosterman} with the smooth weight \[ \Phi\left(x_1, x_2, z\right) := \Psi_0\left(x_1\right) \Psi\left(x_2\right) e\left(\mp x_2\frac{uKB}{C}\right) \Psi_0\left(z\right) \Psi_0\left(uz\right), \] once for each choice of the $\pm$ sign (corresponding to the sign of $k$; note that $S(-fk\overline{s_1 s_2}, a\ell; c) = S(fk\overline{s_1 s_2}, -a\ell; c)$, so one can transfer the sign change to $a$ without loss of generality). This $\Phi$ is compactly supported and satisfies $\partial_{x_1}^{j_1} \partial_{x_2}^{j_2} \partial_z^\ell \Phi(x_1, x_2, z) \ll_{j_1,j_2,k,\ell} (KB/C)^{j_2} \ll x^{o(j_2)}$, where we used $K \ll x^{o(1)} B^{-1} C$ by \cref{eq:W-off-diagonal-split}. Since $\theta_{\max} \le \tfrac{7}{32} = \theta$, we can bound \[ \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_7 &\ll_a x^{o(1)} \frac{B}{C} \left(1 + \frac{C\sqrt{F}}{S^2\sqrt{\frac{H^2}{H+S}}}\right)^{\theta} \\ &\times \sqrt{H^2S^3 (H + S) F K} \left(\frac{C^2}{S}\left(FK + S^2\right)\left(H + S\right) + FKHS\right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \]
nodes.name: Apply Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 4.1 with $\theta_{\max}\le7/32$.

nodes.statement: At this point we note that by \cref{eq:ranges-qrs}, \[ H \le x^{o(1)} \frac{NQ R^2 S^2}{x} \ll x^{o(1)} \frac{N^2 R^2 S}{x} S \ll x^{o(1)} S. \] Using this and the fact that $K \ll x^{o(1)} B^{-1} C$ from \cref{eq:W-off-diagonal-split}, our bound for $\mathscr{W}_7$ simplifies to \[ \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_7 &\ll_a x^{o(1)} \frac{B}{C} \left(1 + \frac{C\sqrt{F}}{S^{3/2} H}\right)^{\theta} \sqrt{H^2S^4 F C / B} \left(C^2\left(FC/B + S^2\right) + FCHS/B\right)^{1/2} \\ &\ll x^{o(1)} \left(1 + \frac{C\sqrt{F}}{S^{3/2} H}\right)^{\theta} \sqrt{H^2S^4 F} \left(C\left(FC + BS^2\right) + FHS\right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \] Plugging in the bounds for $B, C, F$ from \cref{eq:cf-substitution} and \cref{eq:bcf-bounds}, we are left with \[ \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_7 &\ll_a \frac{x^{o(1)}}{d} \left(1 + \frac{C_0\sqrt{F_0}}{S^{3/2} H}\right)^{\theta} \sqrt{H^2S^4 F} \left(C_0\left(FC + BS^2\right) + F_0HS\right)^{1/2} \\ &\ll_a \frac{x^{o(1)}}{d} \left(1 + \frac{NRS \sqrt{N/Q}}{S^{3/2} H}\right)^{\theta} \sqrt{H^2S^4N/Q} \left(NRS \left((N/Q)NRS + NRS^2\right) + (N/Q)HS\right)^{1/2} \\ &= \frac{x^{o(1)}}{d} \left(1 + \frac{N^{3/2} R}{H \sqrt{SQ}}\right)^{\theta} \frac{H S^{5/2} N}{Q} \left(NR^2S \left(N + QS\right) + H\right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \] Finally, noting that the right-hand side is increasing in $H \le x^{o(1)} NQR^2 S^2/x$, we get \[ \begin{aligned} \mathscr{W}_7 &\ll_a \frac{x^{o(1)}}{d} \left(1 + \frac{x\sqrt{N}}{R S^{5/2} Q^{3/2}}\right)^{\theta} \frac{N^2R^2S^{9/2}}{x} \left(N^2R^2S + NQR^2S^2 + \frac{NQR^2 S^2}{x}\right)^{1/2} \\ &\ll_a \frac{x^{o(1)}}{d} \left(1 + \frac{x\sqrt{N}}{R S^{5/2} Q^{3/2}}\right)^{\theta} \frac{N^{5/2} R^3 S^5}{x} \left(N + QS\right)^{1/2} \\ &\ll_{\varepsilon,a} \frac{x^\varepsilon}{d} \left(\frac{N^3 R^3 S^5}{x} \left(1 + \left(\frac{x\sqrt{N}}{R S^{5/2}} \right)^{\theta}\right) + \frac{N^{5/2} Q^{1/2} R^3 S^{11/2}}{x} \left(1 + \left(\frac{x\sqrt{N}}{R S^{5/2} Q^{3/2}} \right)^{\theta}\right)\right), \end{aligned} \] where we omitted a factor of $Q^{-3\theta/2}$ in the second term of the expansion.
nodes.name: Simplify W_7 bound
nodes.statement_short: Use $H\ll S$ and the ranges to simplify the bound for $\mathscr W_7$.

nodes.statement: For this to be acceptable in \cref{eq:W5-bound-to-show} (i.e., $\ll_{\varepsilon,a} x^{-7\varepsilon} N^2 R^2 S^3 / d$), we need the following restrictions: \[ \begin{gathered} N R S^2 \ll x^{1-8\varepsilon}, \qquad\qquad N^{2+\theta} R^{2-2\theta} S^{4-5\theta} \ll x^{2-2\theta-16\varepsilon}, \\ N Q R^2 S^5 \ll x^{2-16\varepsilon}, \qquad\qquad N^{1+\theta} Q^{1-3\theta} R^{2-2\theta} S^{5-5\theta} \ll x^{2-2\theta-16\varepsilon}. \end{gathered} \]
nodes.name: Required restrictions
nodes.statement_short: List the restrictions needed for acceptability.

nodes.statement: All of these restrictions follow from \cref{eq:ranges-qrs}, $Q \ll N$, and $\theta \le 1/2$, as shown below: \[ \begin{aligned} NRS^2 &\le \left(N^2 R^2 S \cdot N R^2 S^5 \right)^{1/3} \le \left(x^{1-8\varepsilon} \cdot x^{2-32\varepsilon}\right)^{1/3} < x^{1-8\varepsilon}, \\ N Q R^2 S^5 &\ll \left(\frac{N}{Q}\right)^{\frac{2\theta}{1-\theta}} N Q R^2 S^5 = N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} Q^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} R^2 S^5 < x^{2-16\varepsilon}, \\ N^{2+\theta} R^{2-2\theta} S^{4-5\theta} &= \left(N^{\frac{2+\theta}{2-2\theta}} R S^{\frac{4-5\theta}{2-2\theta}}\right)^{2-2\theta} \le (x^{1-16\varepsilon})^{2-2\theta} \le x^{2-2\theta-16\varepsilon}, \\ N^{1+\theta} Q^{1-3\theta} R^{2-2\theta} S^{5-5\theta} &= \left(N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} Q^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} R^{2} S^5\right)^{1-\theta} \le (x^{2-32\varepsilon})^{1-\theta} \le x^{2-2\theta-16\varepsilon}. \end{aligned} \] In light of \cref{eq:W5-split,eq:W-diagonal-bound,eq:W-off-diagonal-split,eq:W6-bound}, this establishes \cref{eq:W5-bound-to-show} and completes our proof.
nodes.name: Verify restrictions
nodes.statement_short: Verify the restrictions from (4.5), completing the proof.

nodes.statement: A complex sequence $(a_n)_{n \sim N}$ is said to obey the \emph{Siegel--Walfisz condition} iff one has \[ \sum_{\substack{n \sim N \\ (n, d) = 1}} a_n \left(\mathbbm{1}_{n \equiv a \pmod{q}} - \frac{\mathbbm{1}_{(n, q) = 1}}{\varphi(q)} \right) \ll_A \tau(d)^{O(1)} \frac{N}{(\log N)^A}, \] for all $d, q \in \mathbb{Z}_+$, $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $(a, q) = 1$, and all $A > 1$.
nodes.name: Siegel–Walfisz condition
nodes.label: def:siegel-walfisz

nodes.statement: Let $a \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, $A, \varepsilon > 0$, and $M, N, x, Q_1, Q_2, Q_3 \gg 1$ satisfy $MN \asymp x$ and \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} Q_1 &\le \frac{N}{x^\varepsilon}, \\ N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2 &\le x^{1-15\varepsilon}, \\ N^2 Q_2^5 Q_3^{2} &\le x^{2-40\varepsilon}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Let $(\alpha_n), (\beta_m)$ be $1$-bounded complex sequences, such that $(\alpha_n)$ is supported on $P^-(n) \ge z_0 := x^{1/(\log\log x)^3}$ and satisfies the Siegel--Walfisz condition from \cref{def:siegel-walfisz}. Then for any $1$-bounded complex sequences $(\gamma_{q_1}), (\lambda_{q_2}), (\nu_{q_3})$ supported on $(q_i, a) = 1$, one has \[ \sum_{q_1 \sim Q_1} \gamma_{q_1} \sum_{q_2 \sim Q_2} \lambda_{q_2} \sum_{q_3 \sim Q_3} \nu_{q_3} \sum_{n \sim N} \alpha_n \sum_{m \sim M} \beta_m \left(\mathbbm{1}_{mn \equiv a \pmod{q}} - \frac{\mathbbm{1}_{(mn, q) = 1}}{\varphi(q)}\right) \ll_{\varepsilon,A,a} \frac{x}{(\log x)^A}. \]
nodes.name: Triply-well-factorable convolution estimate
nodes.statement_short: Equidistribution in APs of a convolution $\alpha*\beta$ (with $\alpha$ Siegel–Walfisz) against triple-convolution weights in the ranges (4.15).
assumptions: Let $a \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, $A, \varepsilon > 0$, and $M, N, x, Q_1, Q_2, Q_3 \gg 1$ satisfy $MN \asymp x$ and \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} Q_1 &\le \frac{N}{x^\varepsilon}, \\ N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2 &\le x^{1-15\varepsilon}, \\ N^2 Q_2^5 Q_3^{2} &\le x^{2-40\varepsilon}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Let $(\alpha_n), (\beta_m)$ be $1$-bounded complex sequences, such that $(\alpha_n)$ is supported on $P^-(n) \ge z_0 := x^{1/(\log\log x)^3}$ and satisfies the Siegel--Walfisz condition from \cref{def:siegel-walfisz}.
conclusions: Then for any $1$-bounded complex sequences $(\gamma_{q_1}), (\lambda_{q_2}), (\nu_{q_3})$ supported on $(q_i, a) = 1$, one has \[ \sum_{q_1 \sim Q_1} \gamma_{q_1} \sum_{q_2 \sim Q_2} \lambda_{q_2} \sum_{q_3 \sim Q_3} \nu_{q_3} \sum_{n \sim N} \alpha_n \sum_{m \sim M} \beta_m \left(\mathbbm{1}_{mn \equiv a \pmod{q}} - \frac{\mathbbm{1}_{(mn, q) = 1}}{\varphi(q)}\right) \ll_{\varepsilon,A,a} \frac{x}{(\log x)^A}. \]
nodes.label: prop:well-fact-convolution

nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} Q_1 &\le \frac{N}{x^\varepsilon}, \\ N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2 &\le x^{1-15\varepsilon}, \\ N^2 Q_2^5 Q_3^{2} &\le x^{2-40\varepsilon}. \end{aligned}
nodes.name: Ranges for Q_1, Q_2, Q_3 (4.15)
nodes.label: eq:ranges-q1q2q3-revisited

nodes.statement: From \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3-revisited} we can deduce the slightly-weaker system of inequalities (with $\theta := 7/32$) \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} Q_1 &\le \frac{N}{x^\varepsilon}, \\ N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2 &\le x^{1-9\varepsilon}, \\ N^{\frac{2+\theta}{2-2\theta}} Q_2^{\frac{4-5\theta}{2-2\theta}} Q_3 &\le x^{1-17\varepsilon}, \\ N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_1^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_2^5 Q_3^{2} &\le x^{2-33\varepsilon}, \end{aligned} \end{equation} which will be enough for this proof. Indeed, the third bound in \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3} follows from \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3-revisited} and $(2+\theta)/(2-2\theta) = 71/50$, $(4-5\theta)/(2-2\theta) = 93/50 < 187/100$, since \[ N^{\frac{2+\theta}{2-2\theta}} Q_2^{\frac{4-5\theta}{2-2\theta}} Q_3 \le (N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2)^{21/50} (N^2 Q_2^5 Q_3^2)^{29/100} \le x^{1-17.9\varepsilon}. \] Similarly, the fourth bound in \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3} follows from \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3-revisited} since \[ N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_1^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_2^5 Q_3^2 \le N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} N^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_2^5 Q_3^2 = N^2 Q_2^5 Q_3^2 \le x^{2-40\varepsilon}. \] We now closely follow the proof of \cite[Proposition 7.2]{maynard2025primes2}, which begins by factoring out the $z_0$-smooth parts of $q_2$ and $q_3$ and applying \cite[Proposition 5.8]{maynard2025primes2} (at that step we use $N \ge Q_1 x^\varepsilon$). With $y_0 := x^{1/\log \log x}$, $D \le y_0^2$ and $DR \asymp Q_2 Q_3$, it remains to bound $|\mathscr{E}_1| + |\mathscr{E}_2| \ll \frac{N^2}{DQ_1 y_0}$, where $\mathscr{E}_i$ are the exponential sums from \cite[p.\,26]{maynard2025primes2}. As in \cite[p.\,27]{maynard2025primes2}, the contribution of $\mathscr{E}_1$ is acceptable provided that \[ N^{3/2}Q_2 Q_3 \le x^{1-2\varepsilon}, \qquad\quad Q_1 Q_2 Q_3 \le x^{1-2\varepsilon}, \] both of which follow easily from \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3}. As in \cite[p.\,27]{maynard2025primes2}, to handle $\mathscr{E}_2$ it suffices to bound another exponential sum $\mathscr{E}_3$ by $\mathscr{E}_3 \ll_\varepsilon N^2/(Q_1 x^{\varepsilon/10})$. We note that the range of the $h$ variable can be extended to all $h \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, since the contribution of $|h| > H_2 := (\log x)^5 QDR^2/M$ is negligible. We apply a close variant of \cite[Lemma 5.9]{maynard2025primes2} (which is \cite[Lemma 14.5]{maynard2025primes}) to $\mathscr{E}_3$. Specifically, in the proof of \cite[Lemma 14.5]{maynard2025primes}, we omit the step of applying partial summation in the $h$ variable; instead, we follow the proof of \cref{lem:truncated-poisson} and put $|h|$ in \emph{smooth} dyadic ranges $\Psi(|h|/H')$, bound the contribution of $H' > H_2$ using the decay of $\psi_0$, separate the variables $h$ and $q d r_1 r_2$ variables via a Fourier integral, and fix the integration variable $u \asymp 1$. This produces a smooth factor $\widetilde\psi_0(u q d r_1 r_2 / (QDR^2))$, which we eliminate by partial summation in $q, r_1, r_2$, leading to the exponential sum $\mathscr{E}'$ below. But first, we need to verify the conditions \cite[(5.1), (5.2)]{maynard2025primes2} from \cite[Lemma 5.9]{maynard2025primes2}, \[ Q_1 Q_2 Q_3 \le x^{2/3}, \qquad \qquad Q_1 (Q_2 Q_3)^2 \ll M x^{1-2\varepsilon}, \] both of which follow from \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3}. Indeed, recalling that $MN \asymp x$, we have \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} Q_1 Q_2 Q_3 &\le \left(N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2\right)^{3/8} \left(N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_1^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_2^5 Q_3^2\right)^{1/8} \le \left(x^{1-9\varepsilon}\right)^{3/8} \left(x^{2-33\varepsilon}\right)^{1/8} < x^{5/8}, \\ Q_1 (Q_2 Q_3)^2 &\le \frac{\left(N Q_2 Q_3\right)^2}{N} \le \frac{x^{2-18\varepsilon}}{N} \ll \frac{\left(N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2\right)^2}{N} \ll M x^{1-18\varepsilon}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} As in \cite[p.\,27]{maynard2025primes2}, it remains to bound an exponential sum $\mathscr{E}'$ (roughly corresponding to \cref{eq:sketch-kl-fractions}, before passing to the complementary divisor of $q$) by \begin{equation} \mathscr{E}' \ll_\varepsilon \frac{N^2}{Q_1 x^{\varepsilon/2}}, \end{equation} but we now have \[ \mathscr{E}' := \sum_{\substack{Q_1 \le q \le Q_1' \\ (q, a) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{R \le r_1 \le R_1 \\ R \le r_2 \le R_2 \\ (r_1, ar_2) = 1 \\ (r_2, aqdr_1) = 1}} \frac{\lambda_{r_1} \overline{\lambda_{r_2}}}{qdr_1 r_2} \sum_{\substack{n_1, n_2 \sim N \\ n_1 \equiv n_2 \pmod{qd} \\ (n_1, qdr_1n_2) = 1 \\ (n_2, qdr_2 n_1) = 1 \\ (n_1 r_2, n_2) \in \mathcal{N}}} \alpha_{n_1} \overline{\alpha_{n_2}} \sum_{h \in \mathbb{Z}} e(h\omega)\, \Psi\left(\frac{|h|}{H'}\right) e\left(\frac{ah\overline{n_2qdr_1}(n_1-n_2)}{n_1r_2}\right) , \] where $\Psi : (\frac{1}{2}, 2) \to \mathbb{C}$ is compactly-supported with $\Psi^{(j)} \ll_j 1$, $Q_1' \le 2Q_1$, $R_1, R_2 \le 2R$, $H' \le H_2 = (\log x)^5 QDR^2/M$, and \[ \omega := u \frac{M}{QDR^2} \ll x^{o(1)} H_2^{-1} \qquad\quad \Rightarrow \qquad\quad T_{H'}(\omega) \ll x^{o(1)}. \] All that changed from the sum $\mathscr{E}'$ from \cite[p.\,27]{maynard2025primes2} is that $h$ now lies in a smooth dyadic range, which is ultimately required by our large sieve inequality in \cref{prop:large-sieve-additive}. After expanding $(\lambda_r)$ and fixing one of $x^{o(1)}$ choices of $q_2'', q_3''$, \cref{lem:expo-bound-well-fact} gives the desired bound in \cref{eq:primes-expo-to-bound} provided that \[ \begin{aligned} N^2 {Q_3'}^2 Q_2' &\le x^{1-9\varepsilon}, \\ N^{\frac{2+\theta}{2-2\theta}} Q_3 {Q_2'}^{\frac{4-5\theta}{2-2\theta}} &\le x^{1-17\varepsilon}, \\ N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_1^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} {Q_3'}^{2} {Q_2'}^{5} &\le x^{2-33\varepsilon}, \end{aligned} \] for all $Q_2' \le Q_2$ and $Q_3' \le Q_3$. These bounds follow directly from \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3}, completing our proof.
nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.4
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a weaker range system, then follow Maynard's Proposition 7.2, replacing his exponential sum bound with Lemma 4.2. Key step: putting $h$ in smooth dyadic ranges.

nodes.statement: From \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3-revisited} we can deduce the slightly-weaker system of inequalities (with $\theta := 7/32$) \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} Q_1 &\le \frac{N}{x^\varepsilon}, \\ N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2 &\le x^{1-9\varepsilon}, \\ N^{\frac{2+\theta}{2-2\theta}} Q_2^{\frac{4-5\theta}{2-2\theta}} Q_3 &\le x^{1-17\varepsilon}, \\ N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_1^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_2^5 Q_3^{2} &\le x^{2-33\varepsilon}, \end{aligned} \end{equation} which will be enough for this proof.
nodes.name: Weaker range system
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the weaker system (4.16).

nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} Q_1 &\le \frac{N}{x^\varepsilon}, \\ N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2 &\le x^{1-9\varepsilon}, \\ N^{\frac{2+\theta}{2-2\theta}} Q_2^{\frac{4-5\theta}{2-2\theta}} Q_3 &\le x^{1-17\varepsilon}, \\ N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_1^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_2^5 Q_3^{2} &\le x^{2-33\varepsilon}, \end{aligned}
nodes.name: Equation (4.16) eq:ranges-q1q2q3
nodes.label: eq:ranges-q1q2q3

nodes.statement: Indeed, the third bound in \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3} follows from \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3-revisited} and $(2+\theta)/(2-2\theta) = 71/50$, $(4-5\theta)/(2-2\theta) = 93/50 < 187/100$, since \[ N^{\frac{2+\theta}{2-2\theta}} Q_2^{\frac{4-5\theta}{2-2\theta}} Q_3 \le (N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2)^{21/50} (N^2 Q_2^5 Q_3^2)^{29/100} \le x^{1-17.9\varepsilon}. \] Similarly, the fourth bound in \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3} follows from \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3-revisited} since \[ N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_1^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_2^5 Q_3^2 \le N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} N^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_2^5 Q_3^2 = N^2 Q_2^5 Q_3^2 \le x^{2-40\varepsilon}. \]
nodes.name: Derive the system
nodes.statement_short: Derive the third and fourth bounds of (4.16) by interpolation.

nodes.statement: We now closely follow the proof of \cite[Proposition 7.2]{maynard2025primes2}, which begins by factoring out the $z_0$-smooth parts of $q_2$ and $q_3$ and applying \cite[Proposition 5.8]{maynard2025primes2} (at that step we use $N \ge Q_1 x^\varepsilon$). With $y_0 := x^{1/\log \log x}$, $D \le y_0^2$ and $DR \asymp Q_2 Q_3$, it remains to bound $|\mathscr{E}_1| + |\mathscr{E}_2| \ll \frac{N^2}{DQ_1 y_0}$, where $\mathscr{E}_i$ are the exponential sums from \cite[p.\,26]{maynard2025primes2}.
nodes.name: Follow Maynard Prop. 7.2
nodes.statement_short: Factor out smooth parts and reduce to bounding $\mathscr E_1,\mathscr E_2$.

nodes.statement: As in \cite[p.\,27]{maynard2025primes2}, the contribution of $\mathscr{E}_1$ is acceptable provided that \[ N^{3/2}Q_2 Q_3 \le x^{1-2\varepsilon}, \qquad\quad Q_1 Q_2 Q_3 \le x^{1-2\varepsilon}, \] both of which follow easily from \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3}.
nodes.name: Bound E_1
nodes.statement_short: $\mathscr E_1$ is acceptable under easy range conditions.

nodes.statement: As in \cite[p.\,27]{maynard2025primes2}, to handle $\mathscr{E}_2$ it suffices to bound another exponential sum $\mathscr{E}_3$ by $\mathscr{E}_3 \ll_\varepsilon N^2/(Q_1 x^{\varepsilon/10})$. We note that the range of the $h$ variable can be extended to all $h \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, since the contribution of $|h| > H_2 := (\log x)^5 QDR^2/M$ is negligible.
nodes.name: Reduce E_2 to E_3
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to bound $\mathscr E_3$; extend $h$ to all nonzero integers.

nodes.statement: We apply a close variant of \cite[Lemma 5.9]{maynard2025primes2} (which is \cite[Lemma 14.5]{maynard2025primes}) to $\mathscr{E}_3$. Specifically, in the proof of \cite[Lemma 14.5]{maynard2025primes}, we omit the step of applying partial summation in the $h$ variable; instead, we follow the proof of \cref{lem:truncated-poisson} and put $|h|$ in \emph{smooth} dyadic ranges $\Psi(|h|/H')$, bound the contribution of $H' > H_2$ using the decay of $\psi_0$, separate the variables $h$ and $q d r_1 r_2$ variables via a Fourier integral, and fix the integration variable $u \asymp 1$. This produces a smooth factor $\widetilde\psi_0(u q d r_1 r_2 / (QDR^2))$, which we eliminate by partial summation in $q, r_1, r_2$, leading to the exponential sum $\mathscr{E}'$ below.
nodes.name: Variant of Maynard Lemma 5.9
nodes.statement_short: Put $h$ in smooth dyadic ranges and separate variables, leading to $\mathscr E'$.

nodes.statement: But first, we need to verify the conditions \cite[(5.1), (5.2)]{maynard2025primes2} from \cite[Lemma 5.9]{maynard2025primes2}, \[ Q_1 Q_2 Q_3 \le x^{2/3}, \qquad \qquad Q_1 (Q_2 Q_3)^2 \ll M x^{1-2\varepsilon}, \] both of which follow from \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3}. Indeed, recalling that $MN \asymp x$, we have \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} Q_1 Q_2 Q_3 &\le \left(N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2\right)^{3/8} \left(N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_1^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_2^5 Q_3^2\right)^{1/8} \le \left(x^{1-9\varepsilon}\right)^{3/8} \left(x^{2-33\varepsilon}\right)^{1/8} < x^{5/8}, \\ Q_1 (Q_2 Q_3)^2 &\le \frac{\left(N Q_2 Q_3\right)^2}{N} \le \frac{x^{2-18\varepsilon}}{N} \ll \frac{\left(N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2\right)^2}{N} \ll M x^{1-18\varepsilon}. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.name: Verify conditions (5.1), (5.2)
nodes.statement_short: Check Maynard's conditions from (4.16).

nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} Q_1 Q_2 Q_3 &\le \left(N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2\right)^{3/8} \left(N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_1^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_2^5 Q_3^2\right)^{1/8} \le \left(x^{1-9\varepsilon}\right)^{3/8} \left(x^{2-33\varepsilon}\right)^{1/8} < x^{5/8}, \\ Q_1 (Q_2 Q_3)^2 &\le \frac{\left(N Q_2 Q_3\right)^2}{N} \le \frac{x^{2-18\varepsilon}}{N} \ll \frac{\left(N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2\right)^2}{N} \ll M x^{1-18\varepsilon}. \end{aligned}
nodes.name: Equation (4.17) eq:primes-easy-bounds
nodes.label: eq:primes-easy-bounds

nodes.statement: As in \cite[p.\,27]{maynard2025primes2}, it remains to bound an exponential sum $\mathscr{E}'$ (roughly corresponding to \cref{eq:sketch-kl-fractions}, before passing to the complementary divisor of $q$) by \begin{equation} \mathscr{E}' \ll_\varepsilon \frac{N^2}{Q_1 x^{\varepsilon/2}}, \end{equation} but we now have \[ \mathscr{E}' := \sum_{\substack{Q_1 \le q \le Q_1' \\ (q, a) = 1}} \sum_{\substack{R \le r_1 \le R_1 \\ R \le r_2 \le R_2 \\ (r_1, ar_2) = 1 \\ (r_2, aqdr_1) = 1}} \frac{\lambda_{r_1} \overline{\lambda_{r_2}}}{qdr_1 r_2} \sum_{\substack{n_1, n_2 \sim N \\ n_1 \equiv n_2 \pmod{qd} \\ (n_1, qdr_1n_2) = 1 \\ (n_2, qdr_2 n_1) = 1 \\ (n_1 r_2, n_2) \in \mathcal{N}}} \alpha_{n_1} \overline{\alpha_{n_2}} \sum_{h \in \mathbb{Z}} e(h\omega)\, \Psi\left(\frac{|h|}{H'}\right) e\left(\frac{ah\overline{n_2qdr_1}(n_1-n_2)}{n_1r_2}\right) , \] where $\Psi : (\frac{1}{2}, 2) \to \mathbb{C}$ is compactly-supported with $\Psi^{(j)} \ll_j 1$, $Q_1' \le 2Q_1$, $R_1, R_2 \le 2R$, $H' \le H_2 = (\log x)^5 QDR^2/M$, and \[ \omega := u \frac{M}{QDR^2} \ll x^{o(1)} H_2^{-1} \qquad\quad \Rightarrow \qquad\quad T_{H'}(\omega) \ll x^{o(1)}. \] All that changed from the sum $\mathscr{E}'$ from \cite[p.\,27]{maynard2025primes2} is that $h$ now lies in a smooth dyadic range, which is ultimately required by our large sieve inequality in \cref{prop:large-sieve-additive}.
nodes.name: Define E'
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to bounding $\mathscr E'$ with $h$ in a smooth dyadic range.

nodes.statement: \mathscr{E}' \ll_\varepsilon \frac{N^2}{Q_1 x^{\varepsilon/2}},
nodes.name: Equation (4.18) eq:primes-expo-to-bound
nodes.label: eq:primes-expo-to-bound

nodes.statement: After expanding $(\lambda_r)$ and fixing one of $x^{o(1)}$ choices of $q_2'', q_3''$, \cref{lem:expo-bound-well-fact} gives the desired bound in \cref{eq:primes-expo-to-bound} provided that \[ \begin{aligned} N^2 {Q_3'}^2 Q_2' &\le x^{1-9\varepsilon}, \\ N^{\frac{2+\theta}{2-2\theta}} Q_3 {Q_2'}^{\frac{4-5\theta}{2-2\theta}} &\le x^{1-17\varepsilon}, \\ N^{\frac{1+\theta}{1-\theta}} Q_1^{\frac{1-3\theta}{1-\theta}} {Q_3'}^{2} {Q_2'}^{5} &\le x^{2-33\varepsilon}, \end{aligned} \] for all $Q_2' \le Q_2$ and $Q_3' \le Q_3$. These bounds follow directly from \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3}, completing our proof.
nodes.name: Apply Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.2 bounds $\mathscr E'$ given (4.16).

nodes.statement: The system of inequalities in \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3} is significantly more flexible than the triply-well-factorable condition from \cref{def:triply-well-fact}. In particular, in \cref{sec:primes-linear-sieve}, we will need to use \cref{prop:well-fact-convolution} directly rather than the result below.
nodes.name: Flexibility of the range system

nodes.statement: Let $a \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, $A, \varepsilon > 0$, and $(\lambda_q)$ be triply-well-factorable of level $Q \le x^{5/8-100\varepsilon}$. Let $M, N, x \gg 1$ with $MN \asymp x$ and \[ x^\varepsilon \le N \le x^{3/8}. \] Let $(\alpha_n)$, $(\beta_m)$ be divisor-bounded complex sequences, such that $(\alpha_n)$ is supported on $P^-(n) \ge z_0 := z_0 := x^{1/(\log\log x)^3}$ and satisfies the Siegel--Walfisz condition from \cref{def:siegel-walfisz}. Then for any interval $\mathcal{I} \subset [x, 2x]$, one has \[ \sum_{q \le Q} \lambda_q \sum_{\substack{m \sim M \\ n \sim N \\ mn \in \mathcal{I}}} \alpha_n \beta_m \left(\mathbbm{1}_{mn \equiv a \pmod{q}} - \frac{\mathbbm{1}_{(mn,q) = 1}}{\varphi(q)} \right) \ll_{\varepsilon,A,a} \frac{x}{(\log x)^A}. \]
nodes.name: Triply-well-factorable Type II estimate
nodes.statement_short: Type II estimate for triply-well-factorable weights of level $x^{5/8-100\varepsilon}$ when $x^\varepsilon\le N\le x^{3/8}$.
assumptions: Let $a \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, $A, \varepsilon > 0$, and $(\lambda_q)$ be triply-well-factorable of level $Q \le x^{5/8-100\varepsilon}$. Let $M, N, x \gg 1$ with $MN \asymp x$ and \[ x^\varepsilon \le N \le x^{3/8}. \] Let $(\alpha_n)$, $(\beta_m)$ be divisor-bounded complex sequences, such that $(\alpha_n)$ is supported on $P^-(n) \ge z_0 := z_0 := x^{1/(\log\log x)^3}$ and satisfies the Siegel--Walfisz condition from \cref{def:siegel-walfisz}.
conclusions: Then for any interval $\mathcal{I} \subset [x, 2x]$, one has \[ \sum_{q \le Q} \lambda_q \sum_{\substack{m \sim M \\ n \sim N \\ mn \in \mathcal{I}}} \alpha_n \beta_m \left(\mathbbm{1}_{mn \equiv a \pmod{q}} - \frac{\mathbbm{1}_{(mn,q) = 1}}{\varphi(q)} \right) \ll_{\varepsilon,A,a} \frac{x}{(\log x)^A}. \]
nodes.label: prop:well-fact-type-II

nodes.statement: We follow the proof on \cite[p.\,28]{maynard2025primes2}, reducing to the case of $1$-bounded coefficients via \cite[Lemma 5.1]{maynard2025primes2} and separating the variables $mn$ (from the condition $mn \in \mathcal{I}$) via \cite[Lemma 5.2]{maynard2025primes2}. We may assume that $x^{1/2-\varepsilon} \le Q \le x^{5/8-100\varepsilon}$, since the Bombieri--Vinogradov theorem yields the result for $Q \le x^{1/2-\varepsilon}$. The only difference is that we choose the ranges \[ Q_1 := \frac{N}{x^{\varepsilon}}, \qquad Q_2 := \frac{Q^2}{x^{1-21\varepsilon}}, \qquad Q_3 := \frac{x^{1-20\varepsilon}}{NQ}, \] where we note that $Q_i \ge 1$ since $x^{1/2-\varepsilon} \le Q \le x^{5/8-100\varepsilon}$ and $x^\varepsilon \le N \le x^{3/8}$. We claim that any $Q_1' \le Q_1$, $Q_2' \le Q_2$, $Q_3' \le Q_3$ obey the constraints in \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3-revisited}; indeed, using $Q \le x^{5/8-100\varepsilon}$, we have \[ N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2 = x^{1-19\varepsilon} \le x^{1-15\varepsilon}, \] \[ N^2 Q_2^5 Q_3^{2} = \frac{Q^8}{x^{3-65\varepsilon}} \le x^{2-40\varepsilon}. \] After decomposing the triply-well-factorable weights as in \cref{def:triply-well-fact} and putting $q_i$ in dyadic ranges, \cref{prop:well-fact-convolution} yields the result.
nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.5
nodes.statement_short: Follow Maynard: choose $Q_1,Q_2,Q_3$ explicitly, check (4.15), and apply the convolution estimate.

nodes.statement: We follow the proof on \cite[p.\,28]{maynard2025primes2}, reducing to the case of $1$-bounded coefficients via \cite[Lemma 5.1]{maynard2025primes2} and separating the variables $mn$ (from the condition $mn \in \mathcal{I}$) via \cite[Lemma 5.2]{maynard2025primes2}.
nodes.name: Follow Maynard
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to 1-bounded coefficients and separate $mn$.

nodes.statement: We may assume that $x^{1/2-\varepsilon} \le Q \le x^{5/8-100\varepsilon}$, since the Bombieri--Vinogradov theorem yields the result for $Q \le x^{1/2-\varepsilon}$.
nodes.name: Small Q by Bombieri–Vinogradov
nodes.statement_short: Small $Q$ is covered by Bombieri–Vinogradov.

nodes.statement: The only difference is that we choose the ranges \[ Q_1 := \frac{N}{x^{\varepsilon}}, \qquad Q_2 := \frac{Q^2}{x^{1-21\varepsilon}}, \qquad Q_3 := \frac{x^{1-20\varepsilon}}{NQ}, \] where we note that $Q_i \ge 1$ since $x^{1/2-\varepsilon} \le Q \le x^{5/8-100\varepsilon}$ and $x^\varepsilon \le N \le x^{3/8}$.
nodes.name: Choose Q_1, Q_2, Q_3
nodes.statement_short: Choose explicit ranges $Q_1,Q_2,Q_3$.

nodes.statement: We claim that any $Q_1' \le Q_1$, $Q_2' \le Q_2$, $Q_3' \le Q_3$ obey the constraints in \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3-revisited}; indeed, using $Q \le x^{5/8-100\varepsilon}$, we have \[ N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2 = x^{1-19\varepsilon} \le x^{1-15\varepsilon}, \] \[ N^2 Q_2^5 Q_3^{2} = \frac{Q^8}{x^{3-65\varepsilon}} \le x^{2-40\varepsilon}. \]
nodes.name: Check range system
nodes.statement_short: These ranges satisfy (4.15).

nodes.statement: After decomposing the triply-well-factorable weights as in \cref{def:triply-well-fact} and putting $q_i$ in dyadic ranges, \cref{prop:well-fact-convolution} yields the result.
nodes.name: Apply Proposition 4.4
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the weights and apply Prop. 4.4.

nodes.statement: This is completely analogous to the proof on \cite[p.\,10]{maynard2025primes2}, decomposing the von Mangoldt function via the Heath-Brown identity \cite[Lemma 4.3]{maynard2025primes2}, and noting that $x^{1/3} \le x^{3/8}$. After \cref{prop:well-fact-type-II} handles the critical ranges where some $M_i$ or $N_i$ lies in $[x^\varepsilon, x^{3/8}]$, \cite[Lemma 4.4]{maynard2025primes2} handles the case of one large smooth factor $N_i > x^{3/8}$, while \cite[Proposition 4.2]{maynard2025primes2} handles the case of two large smooth factors $N_i > x^{3/8}$.
nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.3(i)
nodes.statement_short: Heath-Brown identity; critical ranges handled by the Type II estimate, others by Maynard's lemmas.

nodes.statement: For $D \ge 1$, consider the sets of positive integers \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathcal{D}^+(D) &:= \left\{ p_1 \cdots p_r : p_1 \ge \cdots \ge p_r \text{ primes},\, p_1 \cdots p_{j-1} p_j^3 \le D \text{ for odd } j \le r \right\}, \\ \mathcal{D}^-(D) &:= \left\{ p_1 \cdots p_r : p_1 \ge \cdots \ge p_r \text{ primes},\, p_1 \cdots p_{j-1} p_j^3 \le D \text{ for even } j \le r,\, p_1^2 \le D \right\}, \\ \mathcal{D}^{\textnormal{well}}(D) &:= \left\{ p_1 \cdots p_r : p_1 \ge \cdots \ge p_r \text{ primes},\, p_1 \cdots p_{j-1} p_j^2 \le D \text{ for } j \le r \right\}, \end{aligned} \end{equation} which have \[ \mathcal{D}^\pm(D) \subset \mathcal{D}^{\textnormal{well}}(D). \] Similarly, for $r \in \mathbb{Z}_+$, we define the sets of vectors \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbf{D}_r^+(D) &:= \left\{ (P_1, \ldots, P_r) : P_1 \ge \cdots \ge P_r \ge 1,\, P_1 \cdots P_{j-1} P_j^3 \le D \text{ for odd } j \le r \right\}, \\ \mathbf{D}_r^-(D) &:= \left\{ (P_1, \ldots, P_r) : P_1 \ge \cdots \ge P_r \ge 1,\, P_1 \cdots P_{j-1} P_j^3 \le D \text{ for even } j \le r,\, D_1^2 \le D \right\}, \\ \mathbf{D}^{\textnormal{well}}_r(D) &:= \left\{ (P_1, \ldots, P_r) : P_1 \ge \cdots \ge P_r \ge 1,\, P_1 \cdots P_{j-1} P_j^2 \le D \text{ for } j \le r \right\}, \end{aligned} \end{equation} which have \[ \mathbf{D}_r^\pm(D) \subset \mathbf{D}^{\textnormal{well}}_r(D). \]
nodes.name: Linear sieve support
nodes.statement_short: Sets of integers (and vectors) whose ordered prime factors satisfy the upper-, lower-bound and well-factorable linear sieve constraints.
nodes.label: def:linear-sieve

nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathcal{D}^+(D) &:= \left\{ p_1 \cdots p_r : p_1 \ge \cdots \ge p_r \text{ primes},\, p_1 \cdots p_{j-1} p_j^3 \le D \text{ for odd } j \le r \right\}, \\ \mathcal{D}^-(D) &:= \left\{ p_1 \cdots p_r : p_1 \ge \cdots \ge p_r \text{ primes},\, p_1 \cdots p_{j-1} p_j^3 \le D \text{ for even } j \le r,\, p_1^2 \le D \right\}, \\ \mathcal{D}^{\textnormal{well}}(D) &:= \left\{ p_1 \cdots p_r : p_1 \ge \cdots \ge p_r \text{ primes},\, p_1 \cdots p_{j-1} p_j^2 \le D \text{ for } j \le r \right\}, \end{aligned}
nodes.name: Linear sieve support sets (5.1)
nodes.label: eq:linear-sieve-support

nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathbf{D}_r^+(D) &:= \left\{ (P_1, \ldots, P_r) : P_1 \ge \cdots \ge P_r \ge 1,\, P_1 \cdots P_{j-1} P_j^3 \le D \text{ for odd } j \le r \right\}, \\ \mathbf{D}_r^-(D) &:= \left\{ (P_1, \ldots, P_r) : P_1 \ge \cdots \ge P_r \ge 1,\, P_1 \cdots P_{j-1} P_j^3 \le D \text{ for even } j \le r,\, D_1^2 \le D \right\}, \\ \mathbf{D}^{\textnormal{well}}_r(D) &:= \left\{ (P_1, \ldots, P_r) : P_1 \ge \cdots \ge P_r \ge 1,\, P_1 \cdots P_{j-1} P_j^2 \le D \text{ for } j \le r \right\}, \end{aligned}
nodes.name: Linear sieve support vectors (5.2)
nodes.label: eq:linear-sieve-vectors-support

nodes.statement: The \emph{standard} upper-bound ($+$) and lower-bound $(-)$ linear sieve weights of level $D$ are given by \[ \lambda_d^\pm := \mu(d) \cdot \mathbbm{1}_{d \in \mathcal{D}^\pm(D)}. \]
nodes.name: Standard linear sieve weights
nodes.definiendum: standard upper-bound ($+$) and lower-bound $(-)$ linear sieve weights

nodes.statement: There is also a \emph{well-factorable} variant $\widetilde{\lambda}_d^{\pm}$ of these weights due to Iwaniec (see \cite[Chapter 12.7]{friedlander2010opera}, \cite{iwaniec1980new}, \cite[Chapter 8]{maynard2025primes2}), which produces results of essentially the same strength in sieve problems. Given small parameters $\upsilon, \eta > 0$, $\widetilde{\lambda}_d^\pm = \widetilde{\lambda}_d^\pm(\upsilon,\eta)$ is a sum of $O_{\upsilon,\eta}(1)$ sequences of the form \[ \widetilde{\lambda}_{d,\vec{P}}^\pm := \begin{cases} (-1)^r, & d = p_1 \cdots p_r, \, p_j \in (P_j, P_j^{1+\eta}] \text{ primes}, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}, \end{cases} \] where $\vec{P} = (P_1, \ldots, P_r) \in \mathbf{D}_r^\pm(D^{1/(1+\eta)})$ and $P_i$ are part of the sequence $(D^{\upsilon(1+\eta)^j})_{j \ge 0}$.
nodes.name: Well-factorable linear sieve weights
nodes.statement_short: Iwaniec's well-factorable linear sieve weights: sums of $O(1)$ signed indicators of products of primes in prescribed short ranges $(P_j,P_j^{1+\eta}]$.

nodes.statement: Each such sequence is supported on $d \in \mathcal{D}^\pm(D)$, and \emph{well-factorable} in the sense that for \emph{any} choice of $D_1 D_2 = D$ with $D_i \ge 1$, one can write \[ \widetilde{\lambda}_{d,\vec{P}}^\pm = \sum_{d_1 d_2 = d} \alpha_{d_1} \beta_{d_2}, \] for some $1$-bounded sequences $(\alpha_{d_1})$, $(\beta_{d_2})$ supported on $d_i \le D_i$.
nodes.name: Well-factorability of the linear sieve weights
conclusions: Each such sequence is supported on $d \in \mathcal{D}^\pm(D)$, and \emph{well-factorable} in the sense that for \emph{any} choice of $D_1 D_2 = D$ with $D_i \ge 1$, one can write \[ \widetilde{\lambda}_{d,\vec{P}}^\pm = \sum_{d_1 d_2 = d} \alpha_{d_1} \beta_{d_2}, \] for some $1$-bounded sequences $(\alpha_{d_1})$, $(\beta_{d_2})$ supported on $d_i \le D_i$.

nodes.statement: This is inherited from the fact that every $d \in \mathcal{D}^{\textnormal{well}}(D)$ can be greedily factorized as $d = d_1 d_2$, for some positive integers $d_i \le D_i$.
nodes.name: Proof of well-factorability
nodes.statement_short: Greedy factorization of elements of $\mathcal{D}^{\textnormal{well}}(D)$.

nodes.statement: However, the weights $\widetilde\lambda^\pm_d$ are not \emph{triply-well-factorable} in the sense of \cref{def:triply-well-fact}, since not every $d \in \mathcal{D}^\pm(D)$ can be factorized as $d = d_1 d_2 d_3$ with $d_i \le D_i$, given \emph{any} choice of $D_1 D_2 D_3 = D$.
nodes.name: Linear sieve weights are not triply-well-factorable

nodes.statement: Fortunately, to apply our \cref{prop:well-fact-convolution}, it will suffice to use a particular choice of $D_1, D_2, D_3$ which obey the system in \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3-revisited}. Specifically, following \cite{maynard2025primes2,lichtman2023primes}, it will be enough to show that every modulus $d$ of interest has a factorization $d = d_1 d_2 d_3$ into positive integers obeying the system \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} d_1 &\le \frac{N}{x^\delta}, \\ N^2d_2d_3^2 &\le x^{1-\delta}, \\ N^2 d_2^5 d_3^2 &\le x^{2-\delta}, \end{aligned} \end{equation} for some small $\delta > 0$ (compare this with \cref{eq:ranges-q1q2q3-revisited}).
nodes.name: Reduction to a factorization system
nodes.statement_short: It suffices that every modulus factors as $d_1d_2d_3$ satisfying the system (5.3), a special case of (4.15).

nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} d_1 &\le \frac{N}{x^\delta}, \\ N^2d_2d_3^2 &\le x^{1-\delta}, \\ N^2 d_2^5 d_3^2 &\le x^{2-\delta}, \end{aligned}
nodes.name: Factorization system to verify (5.3)
nodes.label: eq:system-to-verify

nodes.statement: Let $0 < \delta < 10^{-5}$, $D = x^{3/5 - 50\delta}$, $x^{2\delta} \le N \le x^{1/3 + \delta}$, and $d \in \mathcal{D}^+(D)$. Then there exists a factorization $d = d_1 d_2 d_3$ into positive integers obeying \cref{eq:system-to-verify}.
nodes.name: Factorization in the upper-bound linear sieve support
nodes.statement_short: Every $d\in\mathcal D^+(x^{3/5-50\delta})$ factors as $d_1d_2d_3$ satisfying system (5.3).
assumptions: Let $0 < \delta < 10^{-5}$, $D = x^{3/5 - 50\delta}$, $x^{2\delta} \le N \le x^{1/3 + \delta}$, and $d \in \mathcal{D}^+(D)$.
conclusions: Then there exists a factorization $d = d_1 d_2 d_3$ into positive integers obeying \cref{eq:system-to-verify}.
nodes.label: prop:fact-upper-linear-sieve

nodes.statement: The level $D = x^{3/5-o(1)}$ in \cref{prop:fact-upper-linear-sieve} is optimal, as seen by taking $N = x^{1/5}$ and $p_1 \approx p_2 \approx x^{1/5}$. There are various other limiting cases, but essentially all situations where $D \le x^{3/5-o(1)}$ can be handled by an interpolation of the ranges \[ d_1 \le N x^{-o(1)}, \qquad\quad d_2 \le x^{1/5 - o(1)}, \qquad\quad d_3 \le \frac{x^{2/5 + o(1)}}{N}, \] and \[ d_1 \le N x^{-o(1)}, \qquad\quad d_2 \le x^{4/15 - o(1)}, \qquad\quad d_3 \le \frac{x^{1/3 + o(1)}}{N}, \] both of which are acceptable in \cref{eq:system-to-verify} (up to a good choice of the $o(1)$ exponents in terms of $\delta$).
nodes.name: Optimality of the level 3/5

nodes.statement: This follows analogously as in \cite[Chapter 8]{maynard2025primes2}, using \cref{prop:well-fact-convolution} instead of \cite[Proposition 7.2]{maynard2025primes2}, and \cref{prop:fact-upper-linear-sieve} instead of \cite[Proposition 8.1]{maynard2025primes2}.
nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.3(ii)
nodes.statement_short: As in Maynard's Chapter 8, with Proposition 4.4 and the new factorization result.

nodes.statement: Let $0 < \delta < 10^{-5}$, $D = x^{3/5 - 50\delta}$, $x^{2\delta} \le N \le x^{1/3 + \delta}$, and $d \in \mathcal{D}^+(D)$ have $6$ prime factors, counting multiplicities. Then there exists a factorization $d = d_1 d_2 d_3$ into positive integers such that \begin{equation} d_1 \le D_1 := N x^{-\delta}, \qquad\quad d_2 \le D_2 := x^{4/15 - 5\delta}, \qquad\quad d_3 \le D_3 := \frac{x^{2/5 + 2\delta}}{N}. \end{equation}
nodes.name: Placing the first 6 prime factors
nodes.statement_short: An element of $\mathcal D^+(D)$ with 6 prime factors splits as $d_1d_2d_3$ with $d_i\le D_i$ as in (5.4).
assumptions: Let $0 < \delta < 10^{-5}$, $D = x^{3/5 - 50\delta}$, $x^{2\delta} \le N \le x^{1/3 + \delta}$, and $d \in \mathcal{D}^+(D)$ have $6$ prime factors, counting multiplicities.
conclusions: Then there exists a factorization $d = d_1 d_2 d_3$ into positive integers such that \begin{equation} d_1 \le D_1 := N x^{-\delta}, \qquad\quad d_2 \le D_2 := x^{4/15 - 5\delta}, \qquad\quad d_3 \le D_3 := \frac{x^{2/5 + 2\delta}}{N}. \end{equation}
nodes.label: lem:placing-first-6

nodes.statement: d_1 \le D_1 := N x^{-\delta}, \qquad\quad d_2 \le D_2 := x^{4/15 - 5\delta}, \qquad\quad d_3 \le D_3 := \frac{x^{2/5 + 2\delta}}{N}.
nodes.name: Bounds D_1, D_2, D_3 (5.4)
nodes.label: eq:linear-sieve-di-bounds

nodes.statement: The values of $D_1, D_2, D_3$ in \cref{eq:linear-sieve-di-bounds} do \emph{not} multiply up to $D$, and do not (yet) obey the conditions on $Q_1, Q_2, Q_3$ from \cref{prop:well-fact-convolution}. So \cref{lem:placing-first-6} does not directly imply \cref{prop:fact-upper-linear-sieve} (not even for integers with $6$ primes factors), but it will be a crucial step in its proof.
nodes.name: Role of the six-prime lemma

nodes.statement: We first observe that $D_1, D_2, D_3 \ge x^\delta$ by the conditions on $N$ and $\delta$. Now let $d \in \mathcal{D}^+(D)$ have prime factorization $d = p_1 \cdots p_6$, with $p_1 \ge \cdots \ge p_6$; in particular, we have \[ p_1^3 \le D, \qquad\quad p_1 p_2 p_3^3 \le D, \qquad\quad p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^3 \le D. \] We claim that it is impossible for the following system of inequalities to hold true simultaneously: \[ \begin{aligned} p_1 p_4 p_5 &> D_2, \\ p_2 p_3 p_5 &> D_2, \\ p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^4 &> D_1 D_2 D_3. \end{aligned} \] Indeed, by multiplying all three inequalities, one would obtain \[ x^{6/5 - 14\delta} = D_1 D_2^3 D_3 < (p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^3)^2 \le D^2, \] which is a contradiction. Thus at least one of these inequalities fails, which leads us to three cases. \underline{\textbf{Case 1:}} $p_1 p_4 p_5 \le D_2$. Then, we fix $d_2 := p_1 p_4 p_5$. We will construct $d_1 \le D_1$ and $d_3 \le D_3$ such that $d_1 d_3 = p_2 p_3 p_6$; for now, we set $d_1 = d_3 := 1$. Since \[ p_2^2 \le p_1^2 \le D^{2/3} \le x^{2/5} \le D_1 D_3, \] we must have $p_2 \le D_1$ or $p_2 \le D_3$; we set $d_1 \gets p_2$ if $p_2 \le D_1$, and $d_3 \gets p_2$ otherwise. We also have \[ p_2 p_3^2 = \left(p_2 p_3^4\right)^{1/2} p_2^{1/2} \le p_1^{1/2} \left(p_1 p_2 p_3^3\right)^{1/2} \le x^{1/10 + 3/10} \le D_1 D_3, \] so $p_3 \le \sqrt{D_1 D_3/(d_1 d_3)}$, which forces $p_3 \le D_1/d_1$ or $p_3 \le D_3/d_3$; we set $d_1 \gets d_1 p_3$ if $p_3 \le D_1/d_1$, and $d_3 \gets d_3 p_3$ otherwise. Finally, we note that \[ p_2 p_3 p_6^2 = p_2^{1/2} \left(p_2 p_3^2 p_6^4\right)^{1/2} \le p_1^{1/2} \left(p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^3\right)^{1/2} \le x^{1/10 + 3/10} \le D_1 D_3, \] so $p_6 \le \sqrt{D_1 D_3/(d_1 d_3)}$, which forces $p_6 \le D_1/d_1$ or $p_6 \le D_3/d_3$; we set $d_1 \gets d_1 p_6$ if $p_6 \le D_1/d_1$, and $d_3 \gets d_3 p_6$ otherwise. At this point, we have $d_1 d_2 d_3 = p_1 \cdots p_6$ and $d_i \le D_i$ for $i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$, as we wanted. \underline{\textbf{Case 2:}} $p_2 p_3 p_5 \le D_2$. Then, we fix $d_2 := p_2 p_3 p_5$, and construct $d_1 \le D_1, d_3 \le D_3$ such that $d_1 d_3 = p_1 p_4 p_6$. The process is completely analogous to the previous case (with $p_1, p_4$ taking the places of $p_2, p_3$), using the bounds \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} p_1 &\le D^{2/3} \le x^{2/5} \le D_1 D_3, \\ p_1 p_4^2 &= \left(p_1 p_4^4\right)^{1/2} p_1^{1/2} \le p_1^{1/2} \left(p_1 p_2 p_3^3\right)^{1/2} \le x^{1/10 + 3/10} \le D_1 D_3, \\ p_1 p_4 p_6^2 &= p_1^{1/2} \left(p_1 p_4^2 p_6^4\right)^{1/2} \le p_1^{1/2} \left(p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^3\right)^{1/2} \le x^{1/10 + 3/10} \le D_1 D_3. \end{aligned} \end{equation} \underline{\textbf{Case 3:}} $p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^4 \le D_1 D_2 D_3$. We can also assume without loss of generality that we are not in the previous case, so $p_2 p_3 p_5 > D_2$. Then, we fix $d_2 := p_2 p_3$, noting that \[ p_2 p_3 \le p_1^{1/3} (p_1 p_2 p_3^3)^{1/3} \le D^{4/9} \le x^{4/15 - 5\delta} = D_2. \] We will construct $d_1 \le D_1$ and $d_3 \le D_3$ such that $d_1 d_3 = p_1 p_4 p_5 p_6$. We start by placing the primes $p_1, p_4, p_6$ into $d_1$ and $d_3$ exactly as in the previous case, using the bounds in \cref{eq:linear-sieve-case-2-bounds}. At this point, we have $d_1 d_3 = p_1 p_4 p_6$, and it remains to place $p_5$. Since \[ p_1 p_4 p_6 p_5^2 \le p_1 p_4 p_5^3 = \frac{p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^4}{p_2 p_3 p_5} \le \frac{D_1 D_2 D_3}{D_2} = D_1 D_3, \] we have $p_5 \le \sqrt{D_1 D_3 / (d_1 d_3)}$, which forces $p_5 \le D_1/d_1$ or $p_5 \le D_3/d_3$. Then we are done by setting $d_i \gets d_i p_5$ for some $i \in \{1, 3\}$.
nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.3
nodes.statement_short: Show three inequalities cannot hold simultaneously, then construct the factorization in each of three cases by greedy placement of primes.

nodes.statement: We first observe that $D_1, D_2, D_3 \ge x^\delta$ by the conditions on $N$ and $\delta$. Now let $d \in \mathcal{D}^+(D)$ have prime factorization $d = p_1 \cdots p_6$, with $p_1 \ge \cdots \ge p_6$; in particular, we have \[ p_1^3 \le D, \qquad\quad p_1 p_2 p_3^3 \le D, \qquad\quad p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^3 \le D. \]
nodes.name: Setup and prime constraints
nodes.statement_short: Note $D_i\ge x^\delta$ and record the constraints on $p_1,\dots,p_6$.

nodes.statement: We claim that it is impossible for the following system of inequalities to hold true simultaneously: \[ \begin{aligned} p_1 p_4 p_5 &> D_2, \\ p_2 p_3 p_5 &> D_2, \\ p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^4 &> D_1 D_2 D_3. \end{aligned} \] Indeed, by multiplying all three inequalities, one would obtain \[ x^{6/5 - 14\delta} = D_1 D_2^3 D_3 < (p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^3)^2 \le D^2, \] which is a contradiction. Thus at least one of these inequalities fails, which leads us to three cases.
nodes.name: Three inequalities cannot all hold
nodes.statement_short: Claim: the three inequalities cannot hold simultaneously.

nodes.statement: Indeed, by multiplying all three inequalities, one would obtain \[ x^{6/5 - 14\delta} = D_1 D_2^3 D_3 < (p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^3)^2 \le D^2, \] which is a contradiction.
nodes.name: Multiply inequalities
nodes.statement_short: Multiplying gives a contradiction with $p_1\cdots p_5^3\le D$.

nodes.statement: Thus at least one of these inequalities fails, which leads us to three cases.
nodes.name: Three cases
nodes.statement_short: Hence one inequality fails, giving three cases.

nodes.statement: \underline{\textbf{Case 1:}} $p_1 p_4 p_5 \le D_2$. Then, we fix $d_2 := p_1 p_4 p_5$. We will construct $d_1 \le D_1$ and $d_3 \le D_3$ such that $d_1 d_3 = p_2 p_3 p_6$; for now, we set $d_1 = d_3 := 1$. Since \[ p_2^2 \le p_1^2 \le D^{2/3} \le x^{2/5} \le D_1 D_3, \] we must have $p_2 \le D_1$ or $p_2 \le D_3$; we set $d_1 \gets p_2$ if $p_2 \le D_1$, and $d_3 \gets p_2$ otherwise. We also have \[ p_2 p_3^2 = \left(p_2 p_3^4\right)^{1/2} p_2^{1/2} \le p_1^{1/2} \left(p_1 p_2 p_3^3\right)^{1/2} \le x^{1/10 + 3/10} \le D_1 D_3, \] so $p_3 \le \sqrt{D_1 D_3/(d_1 d_3)}$, which forces $p_3 \le D_1/d_1$ or $p_3 \le D_3/d_3$; we set $d_1 \gets d_1 p_3$ if $p_3 \le D_1/d_1$, and $d_3 \gets d_3 p_3$ otherwise. Finally, we note that \[ p_2 p_3 p_6^2 = p_2^{1/2} \left(p_2 p_3^2 p_6^4\right)^{1/2} \le p_1^{1/2} \left(p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^3\right)^{1/2} \le x^{1/10 + 3/10} \le D_1 D_3, \] so $p_6 \le \sqrt{D_1 D_3/(d_1 d_3)}$, which forces $p_6 \le D_1/d_1$ or $p_6 \le D_3/d_3$; we set $d_1 \gets d_1 p_6$ if $p_6 \le D_1/d_1$, and $d_3 \gets d_3 p_6$ otherwise. At this point, we have $d_1 d_2 d_3 = p_1 \cdots p_6$ and $d_i \le D_i$ for $i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$, as we wanted.
nodes.name: Case 1
nodes.statement_short: Case $p_1p_4p_5\le D_2$: place $p_2,p_3,p_6$ greedily into $d_1,d_3$.

nodes.statement: Then, we fix $d_2 := p_1 p_4 p_5$. We will construct $d_1 \le D_1$ and $d_3 \le D_3$ such that $d_1 d_3 = p_2 p_3 p_6$; for now, we set $d_1 = d_3 := 1$.
nodes.name: Fix d_2
nodes.statement_short: Set $d_2=p_1p_4p_5$ and start with $d_1=d_3=1$.

nodes.statement: Since \[ p_2^2 \le p_1^2 \le D^{2/3} \le x^{2/5} \le D_1 D_3, \] we must have $p_2 \le D_1$ or $p_2 \le D_3$; we set $d_1 \gets p_2$ if $p_2 \le D_1$, and $d_3 \gets p_2$ otherwise.
nodes.name: Place p_2
nodes.statement_short: Place $p_2$ using $p_2^2\le D_1D_3$.

nodes.statement: We also have \[ p_2 p_3^2 = \left(p_2 p_3^4\right)^{1/2} p_2^{1/2} \le p_1^{1/2} \left(p_1 p_2 p_3^3\right)^{1/2} \le x^{1/10 + 3/10} \le D_1 D_3, \] so $p_3 \le \sqrt{D_1 D_3/(d_1 d_3)}$, which forces $p_3 \le D_1/d_1$ or $p_3 \le D_3/d_3$; we set $d_1 \gets d_1 p_3$ if $p_3 \le D_1/d_1$, and $d_3 \gets d_3 p_3$ otherwise.
nodes.name: Place p_3
nodes.statement_short: Place $p_3$ using $p_2p_3^2\le D_1D_3$.

nodes.statement: Finally, we note that \[ p_2 p_3 p_6^2 = p_2^{1/2} \left(p_2 p_3^2 p_6^4\right)^{1/2} \le p_1^{1/2} \left(p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^3\right)^{1/2} \le x^{1/10 + 3/10} \le D_1 D_3, \] so $p_6 \le \sqrt{D_1 D_3/(d_1 d_3)}$, which forces $p_6 \le D_1/d_1$ or $p_6 \le D_3/d_3$; we set $d_1 \gets d_1 p_6$ if $p_6 \le D_1/d_1$, and $d_3 \gets d_3 p_6$ otherwise.
nodes.name: Place p_6
nodes.statement_short: Place $p_6$ using $p_2p_3p_6^2\le D_1D_3$.

nodes.statement: At this point, we have $d_1 d_2 d_3 = p_1 \cdots p_6$ and $d_i \le D_i$ for $i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$, as we wanted.
nodes.name: Factorization found
nodes.statement_short: All bounds $d_i\le D_i$ hold.

nodes.statement: \underline{\textbf{Case 2:}} $p_2 p_3 p_5 \le D_2$. Then, we fix $d_2 := p_2 p_3 p_5$, and construct $d_1 \le D_1, d_3 \le D_3$ such that $d_1 d_3 = p_1 p_4 p_6$. The process is completely analogous to the previous case (with $p_1, p_4$ taking the places of $p_2, p_3$), using the bounds \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} p_1 &\le D^{2/3} \le x^{2/5} \le D_1 D_3, \\ p_1 p_4^2 &= \left(p_1 p_4^4\right)^{1/2} p_1^{1/2} \le p_1^{1/2} \left(p_1 p_2 p_3^3\right)^{1/2} \le x^{1/10 + 3/10} \le D_1 D_3, \\ p_1 p_4 p_6^2 &= p_1^{1/2} \left(p_1 p_4^2 p_6^4\right)^{1/2} \le p_1^{1/2} \left(p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^3\right)^{1/2} \le x^{1/10 + 3/10} \le D_1 D_3. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.name: Case 2
nodes.statement_short: Case $p_2p_3p_5\le D_2$: analogous, using (5.5).

nodes.statement: \underline{\textbf{Case 3:}} $p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^4 \le D_1 D_2 D_3$. We can also assume without loss of generality that we are not in the previous case, so $p_2 p_3 p_5 > D_2$. Then, we fix $d_2 := p_2 p_3$, noting that \[ p_2 p_3 \le p_1^{1/3} (p_1 p_2 p_3^3)^{1/3} \le D^{4/9} \le x^{4/15 - 5\delta} = D_2. \] We will construct $d_1 \le D_1$ and $d_3 \le D_3$ such that $d_1 d_3 = p_1 p_4 p_5 p_6$. We start by placing the primes $p_1, p_4, p_6$ into $d_1$ and $d_3$ exactly as in the previous case, using the bounds in \cref{eq:linear-sieve-case-2-bounds}. At this point, we have $d_1 d_3 = p_1 p_4 p_6$, and it remains to place $p_5$. Since \[ p_1 p_4 p_6 p_5^2 \le p_1 p_4 p_5^3 = \frac{p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^4}{p_2 p_3 p_5} \le \frac{D_1 D_2 D_3}{D_2} = D_1 D_3, \] we have $p_5 \le \sqrt{D_1 D_3 / (d_1 d_3)}$, which forces $p_5 \le D_1/d_1$ or $p_5 \le D_3/d_3$. Then we are done by setting $d_i \gets d_i p_5$ for some $i \in \{1, 3\}$.
nodes.name: Case 3
nodes.statement_short: Case $p_1\cdots p_5^4\le D_1D_2D_3$: set $d_2=p_2p_3$ and place the rest.

nodes.statement: We can also assume without loss of generality that we are not in the previous case, so $p_2 p_3 p_5 > D_2$.
nodes.name: Not in Case 2
nodes.statement_short: WLOG $p_2p_3p_5>D_2$.

nodes.statement: Then, we fix $d_2 := p_2 p_3$, noting that \[ p_2 p_3 \le p_1^{1/3} (p_1 p_2 p_3^3)^{1/3} \le D^{4/9} \le x^{4/15 - 5\delta} = D_2. \] We will construct $d_1 \le D_1$ and $d_3 \le D_3$ such that $d_1 d_3 = p_1 p_4 p_5 p_6$. We start by placing the primes $p_1, p_4, p_6$ into $d_1$ and $d_3$ exactly as in the previous case, using the bounds in \cref{eq:linear-sieve-case-2-bounds}.
nodes.name: Fix d_2 = p_2 p_3
nodes.statement_short: Set $d_2=p_2p_3\le D_2$ and place $p_1,p_4,p_6$ as before.

nodes.statement: At this point, we have $d_1 d_3 = p_1 p_4 p_6$, and it remains to place $p_5$. Since \[ p_1 p_4 p_6 p_5^2 \le p_1 p_4 p_5^3 = \frac{p_1 p_2 p_3 p_4 p_5^4}{p_2 p_3 p_5} \le \frac{D_1 D_2 D_3}{D_2} = D_1 D_3, \] we have $p_5 \le \sqrt{D_1 D_3 / (d_1 d_3)}$, which forces $p_5 \le D_1/d_1$ or $p_5 \le D_3/d_3$. Then we are done by setting $d_i \gets d_i p_5$ for some $i \in \{1, 3\}$.
nodes.name: Place p_5
nodes.statement_short: Place $p_5$ using $p_1p_4p_6p_5^2\le D_1D_3$.

nodes.statement: Let $d \in \mathcal{D}^+(D)$ have prime factorization $d = p_1 \cdots p_r$ with $p_1 \ge p_2 \ge \ldots$. We recall from \cref{eq:linear-sieve-support} that this implies \[ p_1 \cdots p_{2j} p_{2j+1}^3 \le D \qquad\quad \text{and} \qquad\quad p_1 \cdots p_{k-1} p_k^2 \le D, \] for all $0 \le k < r/2$ and $1 \le k \le r$. We aim to place the primes $p_1, \ldots, p_r$ into $d_1, d_2, d_3$ such that the bounds in \cref{eq:system-to-verify} hold. We begin by setting $d_1 = d_2 = d_3 := 1$, and perform the following iterative greedy process. At step $1 \le j \le r$, we do the following: \begin{itemize} \item[$j.(i)$.] If $j \le 6$, we place $p_j$ in the corresponding factor $d_i$ from the factorization in \cref{lem:placing-first-6} (i.e., we set $d_i \gets d_i p_j$). If $j \ge 7$, we act greedily and place $p_j$ into any factor $d_i$ such that after substituting $d_i \gets d_i p_j$, we have the same system of inequalities \[ d_1 \le N x^{-\delta}, \qquad\quad d_2 \le x^{4/15 - 5\delta}, \qquad\quad d_3 \le \frac{x^{2/5 + 2\delta}}{N}, \] as in \cref{eq:linear-sieve-di-bounds}. We terminate unsuccessfully if this is impossible. \item[$j.(ii)$.] Having placed $p_j$ into some $d_i$, we check whether either of the lower bounds \[ d_2 > x^{1/5 - 5\delta}, \qquad\quad \text{or} \qquad\quad d_3 > \frac{x^{1/3 + 2\delta}}{N}, \] holds; if so, we terminate unsuccessfully. Otherwise, we continue with step $j+1$ (or terminate successfully if $j = r$). \end{itemize} \underline{\textbf{Case 1:}} The process terminates successfully; this is the easier case. We are left with a factorization $d = d_1 d_2 d_3$ satisfying \[ d_1 \le N x^{-\delta}, \qquad\quad d_2 \le x^{1/5-5\delta}, \qquad\quad d_3 \le \frac{x^{1/3+2\delta}}{N}, \] which actually forces $d \le x^{8/15 - 4\delta}$ (significantly smaller than $D = x^{9/15 - 50\delta}$). Then we can verify the conditions in \cref{eq:system-to-verify}, with room to spare: \[ N^2 d_2 d_3^2 \le x^{2(1/3 + 2\delta) + (1/5 - 5\delta)} < x^{1-\delta}, \] \[ N^2 d_2^5 d_3^2 \le x^{2(1/3+2\delta) + (1-25\delta)} \le x^{2-\delta}. \] \underline{\textbf{Case 2:}} The process terminates unsuccessfully in substep $j.(i)$; we show that this cannot happen. Indeed, we must have $j \ge 7$ since \cref{lem:placing-first-6} handles all $j \le 6$. We are left with a factorization $p_1 \cdots p_{j-1} = d_1 d_2 d_3$, which must satisfy \[ d_2 p_j > x^{4/15-5\delta}, \] in order to terminate in substep $j.(i)$. Moreover, since we did not terminate in substep $(j-1).(ii)$, we must have \[ d_2 \le x^{1/5 - 5\delta}. \] But since $j \ge 7$, we have \[ \frac{x^{4/15-5\delta}}{x^{1/5-5\delta}} < \frac{d_2 p_j}{d_2} \le p_7 \le \left(p_1 \cdots p_6 p_7^3\right)^{1/9} \le D^{1/9} < x^{1/15}, \] which gives a contradiction. \underline{\textbf{Case 3:}} The process terminates unsuccessfully in substep $j.(ii)$; this is the main case. We are left with a factorization $p_1 \cdots p_j = d_1 d_2 d_3$ satisfying \begin{equation} d_1 \le N x^{-\delta}, \qquad\quad d_2 \le x^{4/15 - 5\delta}, \qquad\quad d_3 \le \frac{x^{2/5 + 2\delta}}{N}, \end{equation} and \emph{either} $d_2 > x^{1/5-5\delta}$ \emph{or} $d_3 > x^{1/3+2\delta}/N$ (we cannot have both, since we should have terminated in a previous substep $(ii)$ in that case; note that both of these bounds fail at the very beginning of the greedy process because $N \le x^{1/3+\delta}$, and that only one $d_i$ gets updated in each substep $(i)$). \emph{Case 3.1:} If $d_2 > x^{1/5 - 5\delta}$ and $d_3 \le x^{1/3+2\delta}/N$, we set $D_1 := Nx^{-\delta}$, $D_2 := d_2$, and $D_3 := x^{3/5 - 3\delta}/(Nd_2)$, which have $D_i \ge d_i$ (in light of \cref{eq:fact-satisfying}) and $D_1 D_2 D_3 \ge D$. We then run a greedy process to place the remaining primes $p_k$ with $k \ge j+1$ into either $d_1$ or $d_3$, while preserving the inequalities $d_i \le D_i$. This works because at step $k$, before placing $p_k$, we have \[ p_1 \cdots p_{k-1} p_k^2 \le D \qquad\quad \Rightarrow \qquad\quad p_k^2 \le \frac{D}{d_1 d_2 d_3} \le \frac{D_1 D_3}{d_1 d_3}, \] so $p_k \le \max(D_1/d_1, D_3/d_3)$ (i.e., there is ``enough room'' for $p_k$ in $d_1$ or $d_3$). In the end, we have $d = d_1 d_2 d_3$ with $d_i \le D_i$, and we can verify the bounds in \cref{eq:system-to-verify} using $x^{1/5 - 5\delta} < d_2 \le x^{4/15-5\delta}$: \[ N^2 d_2 d_3^2 \le N^2 d_2 \left(\frac{x^{3/5-3\delta}}{Nd_2}\right)^2 = \frac{x^{6/5 - 6\delta}}{d_2} < x^{1-\delta}, \] \[ N^2 d_2^5 d_3^2 \le N^2 d_2^5 \left(\frac{x^{3/5-3\delta}}{Nd_2}\right)^2 = d_2^3 x^{6/5-6\delta} \le x^{2-\delta}. \] \emph{Case 3.2:} Otherwise, we have $d_2 \le x^{1/5-5\delta}$ and $d_3 > x^{1/3+2\delta}/N$. We then set $D_1 := N x^{-\delta}$, $D_2 := x^{3/5-3\delta}/(Nd_3)$, and $D_3 := d_3$, which have $D_i \ge d_i$ (in light of \cref{eq:fact-satisfying}) and $D_1 D_2 D_3 \ge D$. We run a similar greedy process to place the remaining primes $p_k$ with $k \ge j+1$ into either $d_1$ or $d_2$, while preserving the bounds $d_i \le D_i$. This works because at step $k$, before placing $p_k$, we have \[ p_1 \cdots p_{k-1} p_k^2 \le D \qquad\quad \Rightarrow \qquad\quad p_k^2 \le \frac{D}{d_1 d_2 d_3} \le \frac{D_1 D_2}{d_1 d_2}, \] so $p_k \le \max(\frac{D_1}{d_1}, \frac{D_2}{d_2})$. In the end, we have $d = d_1 d_2 d_3$ with $d_i \le D_i$, and we can verify the bounds in \cref{eq:system-to-verify} using $x^{1/3 + 2\delta}/N < d_3 \le x^{2/5 + 2\delta}/N$: \[ N^2 d_2 d_3^2 \le N^2 \frac{x^{3/5-3\delta}}{Nd_3} d_3^2 = N d_3\, x^{3/5 - 3\delta} \le x^{1-\delta}, \] \[ N^2 d_2^5 d_3^2 \le N^2 \left(\frac{x^{3/5-3\delta}}{Nd_3}\right)^5 d_3^2 = \frac{x^{3-15\delta}}{(Nd_3)^3} \le x^{2-\delta}. \] We have now covered all cases.
nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.2
nodes.statement_short: Run a greedy placement starting from Lemma 5.3, and analyse the three ways it can terminate. Key step: when it stops early, enlarge $D_3$ or $D_2$ and finish greedily.

nodes.statement: Let $d \in \mathcal{D}^+(D)$ have prime factorization $d = p_1 \cdots p_r$ with $p_1 \ge p_2 \ge \ldots$. We recall from \cref{eq:linear-sieve-support} that this implies \[ p_1 \cdots p_{2j} p_{2j+1}^3 \le D \qquad\quad \text{and} \qquad\quad p_1 \cdots p_{k-1} p_k^2 \le D, \] for all $0 \le k < r/2$ and $1 \le k \le r$. We aim to place the primes $p_1, \ldots, p_r$ into $d_1, d_2, d_3$ such that the bounds in \cref{eq:system-to-verify} hold.
nodes.name: Setup
nodes.statement_short: Recall the constraints from the definition of $\mathcal D^+(D)$.

nodes.statement: We begin by setting $d_1 = d_2 = d_3 := 1$, and perform the following iterative greedy process. At step $1 \le j \le r$, we do the following:
nodes.name: Greedy process
nodes.statement_short: Start an iterative greedy placement of primes.

nodes.statement: [$j.(i)$.] If $j \le 6$, we place $p_j$ in the corresponding factor $d_i$ from the factorization in \cref{lem:placing-first-6} (i.e., we set $d_i \gets d_i p_j$). If $j \ge 7$, we act greedily and place $p_j$ into any factor $d_i$ such that after substituting $d_i \gets d_i p_j$, we have the same system of inequalities \[ d_1 \le N x^{-\delta}, \qquad\quad d_2 \le x^{4/15 - 5\delta}, \qquad\quad d_3 \le \frac{x^{2/5 + 2\delta}}{N}, \] as in \cref{eq:linear-sieve-di-bounds}. We terminate unsuccessfully if this is impossible.
nodes.name: Substep j.(i)
nodes.statement_short: Place $p_j$ per Lemma 5.3 for $j\le6$, greedily afterwards.

nodes.statement: [$j.(ii)$.] Having placed $p_j$ into some $d_i$, we check whether either of the lower bounds \[ d_2 > x^{1/5 - 5\delta}, \qquad\quad \text{or} \qquad\quad d_3 > \frac{x^{1/3 + 2\delta}}{N}, \] holds; if so, we terminate unsuccessfully. Otherwise, we continue with step $j+1$ (or terminate successfully if $j = r$).
nodes.name: Substep j.(ii)
nodes.statement_short: Stop if $d_2$ or $d_3$ exceeds its lower threshold.

nodes.statement: \underline{\textbf{Case 1:}} The process terminates successfully; this is the easier case. We are left with a factorization $d = d_1 d_2 d_3$ satisfying \[ d_1 \le N x^{-\delta}, \qquad\quad d_2 \le x^{1/5-5\delta}, \qquad\quad d_3 \le \frac{x^{1/3+2\delta}}{N}, \] which actually forces $d \le x^{8/15 - 4\delta}$ (significantly smaller than $D = x^{9/15 - 50\delta}$). Then we can verify the conditions in \cref{eq:system-to-verify}, with room to spare: \[ N^2 d_2 d_3^2 \le x^{2(1/3 + 2\delta) + (1/5 - 5\delta)} < x^{1-\delta}, \] \[ N^2 d_2^5 d_3^2 \le x^{2(1/3+2\delta) + (1-25\delta)} \le x^{2-\delta}. \]
nodes.name: Case 1: success
nodes.statement_short: If the process succeeds, (5.3) holds with room to spare.

nodes.statement: \underline{\textbf{Case 2:}} The process terminates unsuccessfully in substep $j.(i)$; we show that this cannot happen. Indeed, we must have $j \ge 7$ since \cref{lem:placing-first-6} handles all $j \le 6$. We are left with a factorization $p_1 \cdots p_{j-1} = d_1 d_2 d_3$, which must satisfy \[ d_2 p_j > x^{4/15-5\delta}, \] in order to terminate in substep $j.(i)$. Moreover, since we did not terminate in substep $(j-1).(ii)$, we must have \[ d_2 \le x^{1/5 - 5\delta}. \] But since $j \ge 7$, we have \[ \frac{x^{4/15-5\delta}}{x^{1/5-5\delta}} < \frac{d_2 p_j}{d_2} \le p_7 \le \left(p_1 \cdots p_6 p_7^3\right)^{1/9} \le D^{1/9} < x^{1/15}, \] which gives a contradiction.
nodes.name: Case 2: impossible
nodes.statement_short: Termination in substep (i) contradicts $p_7\le D^{1/9}$.

nodes.statement: \underline{\textbf{Case 3:}} The process terminates unsuccessfully in substep $j.(ii)$; this is the main case. We are left with a factorization $p_1 \cdots p_j = d_1 d_2 d_3$ satisfying \begin{equation} d_1 \le N x^{-\delta}, \qquad\quad d_2 \le x^{4/15 - 5\delta}, \qquad\quad d_3 \le \frac{x^{2/5 + 2\delta}}{N}, \end{equation} and \emph{either} $d_2 > x^{1/5-5\delta}$ \emph{or} $d_3 > x^{1/3+2\delta}/N$ (we cannot have both, since we should have terminated in a previous substep $(ii)$ in that case; note that both of these bounds fail at the very beginning of the greedy process because $N \le x^{1/3+\delta}$, and that only one $d_i$ gets updated in each substep $(i)$). \emph{Case 3.1:} If $d_2 > x^{1/5 - 5\delta}$ and $d_3 \le x^{1/3+2\delta}/N$, we set $D_1 := Nx^{-\delta}$, $D_2 := d_2$, and $D_3 := x^{3/5 - 3\delta}/(Nd_2)$, which have $D_i \ge d_i$ (in light of \cref{eq:fact-satisfying}) and $D_1 D_2 D_3 \ge D$. We then run a greedy process to place the remaining primes $p_k$ with $k \ge j+1$ into either $d_1$ or $d_3$, while preserving the inequalities $d_i \le D_i$. This works because at step $k$, before placing $p_k$, we have \[ p_1 \cdots p_{k-1} p_k^2 \le D \qquad\quad \Rightarrow \qquad\quad p_k^2 \le \frac{D}{d_1 d_2 d_3} \le \frac{D_1 D_3}{d_1 d_3}, \] so $p_k \le \max(D_1/d_1, D_3/d_3)$ (i.e., there is ``enough room'' for $p_k$ in $d_1$ or $d_3$). In the end, we have $d = d_1 d_2 d_3$ with $d_i \le D_i$, and we can verify the bounds in \cref{eq:system-to-verify} using $x^{1/5 - 5\delta} < d_2 \le x^{4/15-5\delta}$: \[ N^2 d_2 d_3^2 \le N^2 d_2 \left(\frac{x^{3/5-3\delta}}{Nd_2}\right)^2 = \frac{x^{6/5 - 6\delta}}{d_2} < x^{1-\delta}, \] \[ N^2 d_2^5 d_3^2 \le N^2 d_2^5 \left(\frac{x^{3/5-3\delta}}{Nd_2}\right)^2 = d_2^3 x^{6/5-6\delta} \le x^{2-\delta}. \] \emph{Case 3.2:} Otherwise, we have $d_2 \le x^{1/5-5\delta}$ and $d_3 > x^{1/3+2\delta}/N$. We then set $D_1 := N x^{-\delta}$, $D_2 := x^{3/5-3\delta}/(Nd_3)$, and $D_3 := d_3$, which have $D_i \ge d_i$ (in light of \cref{eq:fact-satisfying}) and $D_1 D_2 D_3 \ge D$. We run a similar greedy process to place the remaining primes $p_k$ with $k \ge j+1$ into either $d_1$ or $d_2$, while preserving the bounds $d_i \le D_i$. This works because at step $k$, before placing $p_k$, we have \[ p_1 \cdots p_{k-1} p_k^2 \le D \qquad\quad \Rightarrow \qquad\quad p_k^2 \le \frac{D}{d_1 d_2 d_3} \le \frac{D_1 D_2}{d_1 d_2}, \] so $p_k \le \max(\frac{D_1}{d_1}, \frac{D_2}{d_2})$. In the end, we have $d = d_1 d_2 d_3$ with $d_i \le D_i$, and we can verify the bounds in \cref{eq:system-to-verify} using $x^{1/3 + 2\delta}/N < d_3 \le x^{2/5 + 2\delta}/N$: \[ N^2 d_2 d_3^2 \le N^2 \frac{x^{3/5-3\delta}}{Nd_3} d_3^2 = N d_3\, x^{3/5 - 3\delta} \le x^{1-\delta}, \] \[ N^2 d_2^5 d_3^2 \le N^2 \left(\frac{x^{3/5-3\delta}}{Nd_3}\right)^5 d_3^2 = \frac{x^{3-15\delta}}{(Nd_3)^3} \le x^{2-\delta}. \] We have now covered all cases.
nodes.name: Case 3: main case
nodes.statement_short: Termination in substep (ii): enlarge one factor bound and finish greedily.

nodes.statement: The process terminates unsuccessfully in substep $j.(ii)$; this is the main case. We are left with a factorization $p_1 \cdots p_j = d_1 d_2 d_3$ satisfying \begin{equation} d_1 \le N x^{-\delta}, \qquad\quad d_2 \le x^{4/15 - 5\delta}, \qquad\quad d_3 \le \frac{x^{2/5 + 2\delta}}{N}, \end{equation} and \emph{either} $d_2 > x^{1/5-5\delta}$ \emph{or} $d_3 > x^{1/3+2\delta}/N$ (we cannot have both, since we should have terminated in a previous substep $(ii)$ in that case; note that both of these bounds fail at the very beginning of the greedy process because $N \le x^{1/3+\delta}$, and that only one $d_i$ gets updated in each substep $(i)$).
